title.zh: 卷二十二 魏書二十二 桓二陳徐衛盧傳
title.en: Volume 22: Book of Wei 22 - Biographies of Huan, the two Chens, Xu, Wei, and Lu
title.raw: 卷二十二 魏書二十二 桓二陳徐衛盧傳 Volume 22: Book of Wei 22 - Biographies of Huan, the two Chens, Xu, Wei, and Lu

sentences.zh: 桓阶 陈群 陈矫 徐宣 卫臻 卢毓

translations.literal: Huan Jie, Chen Qun, Chen Jiao, Xu Xuan, Wei Zhen, and Lu Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Jie, Chen Qun, Chen Jiao, Xu Xuan, Wei Zhen, and Lu Yu.

sentences.zh: 桓階字伯緒，長沙臨湘人也。

translations.literal: Huan Jie, courtesy name Bozhu, was a native of Linxiang in Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Jie, whose courtesy name was Bozhu, came from Linxiang in Changsha commandery.

sentences.zh: 〈魏书曰：阶祖父超，父胜，皆历典州郡。

translations.literal: The Book of Wei states: Jie's grandfather Chao and his father Sheng had both successively held office governing commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: According to the Book of Wei, Jie's grandfather Chao and his father Sheng had each served in turn as administrators of commanderies.

sentences.zh: 胜为尚书，著名南方。〉

translations.literal: Sheng became a secretary in the Masters of Writing and was renowned in the south.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng rose to secretary in the Masters of Writing and won a reputation throughout the south.

sentences.zh: 仕郡功曹。

translations.literal: He served as merit clerk in his commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He held the post of merit clerk in his home commandery.

sentences.zh: 太守孫堅舉階孝廉，除尚書郎。

translations.literal: The grand warden Sun Jian recommended Jie as filial and incorrupt, and he was appointed gentleman of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Warden Sun Jian nominated him as filial and incorrupt, after which he received appointment as a gentleman of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 父喪還鄉里。

translations.literal: When his father died he returned to his home village.
translations.idiomatic: On his father's death he went home to observe mourning.

sentences.zh: 會堅擊劉表戰死，階冒難詣表乞堅喪，表義而與之。

translations.literal: It happened that Sun Jian was killed fighting Liu Biao; braving danger Jie went to Biao to beg for Sun Jian's remains, and Biao, moved by his sense of duty, granted them.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jian had fallen in battle against Liu Biao; Jie risked his life to petition Biao for the body, and Biao, respecting his loyalty, handed it over.

sentences.zh: 後太祖與袁紹相拒於官渡，表舉州以應紹。

translations.literal: Later, when the Grand Progenitor and Yuan Shao faced each other at Guandu, Biao raised the whole province to answer Shao.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as the Grand Progenitor locked horns with Yuan Shao at Guandu, Liu Biao mobilized the entire province in Shao's support.

sentences.zh: 階說其太守張羡曰：「夫舉事而不本於義，未有不敗者也。

translations.literal: Jie urged his grand warden Zhang Xian, saying, 'When one undertakes an affair without rooting it in righteousness, there has never been one who did not fail.'
translations.idiomatic: Jie remonstrated with Grand Warden Zhang Xian: 'Launch a venture without anchoring it in right principle, and ruin follows every time.'

sentences.zh: 故齊桓率諸侯以尊周，晉文逐叔帶以納王。

translations.literal: Therefore Duke Huan of Qi led the feudal lords to honor the Zhou house, and Duke Wen of Jin drove out Shudai to restore the king.
translations.idiomatic: Think of how Duke Huan of Qi rallied the lords to uphold the Zhou, and Duke Wen of Jin expelled Shudai to escort the king back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 今袁氏反此，而劉牧應之，取禍之道也。

translations.literal: Now the Yuan clan has turned this pattern on its head, yet Governor Liu answers their call—that is the road to disaster.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuans have inverted that example, and Governor Liu is marching with them straight toward calamity.

sentences.zh: 明府必欲立功明義，全福遠禍，不宜與之同也。

translations.literal: If you, sir, truly wish to achieve merit and make righteousness clear, preserving good fortune and keeping harm far away, you ought not to go along with them.
translations.idiomatic: If you mean to win real merit, show where justice lies, secure lasting good fortune, and steer clear of ruin, you must not march in their company.

sentences.zh: 」羡曰：「然則何向而可？

translations.literal: Zhang Xian said, 'Then toward whom should we turn to be in the right?'
translations.idiomatic: Xian asked, 'In that case, whom should we follow?'

sentences.zh: 」階曰：「曹公雖弱，仗義而起，救朝廷之危，奉王命而討有罪，孰敢不服？

translations.literal: Jie replied, 'Lord Cao may seem weak, but he rose in the cause of righteousness, rescued the court from peril, and marches under the king's mandate to punish the guilty—who would dare refuse to submit?
translations.idiomatic: Jie answered, 'Lord Cao looks outmatched, yet he took up arms for the right, delivered the throne from danger, and now campaigns with imperial sanction against criminals—who could withhold allegiance?'

sentences.zh: 今若舉四郡保三江以待其來，而爲之内應，不亦可乎！

translations.literal: If we now raise the four commanderies, hold the three river lines, and await his arrival while acting as his allies within, would that not be fitting?'
translations.idiomatic: Raise the four southern commanderies, guard the three river approaches, wait for his host, and strike from within as his confederates—would that not serve?'

sentences.zh: 」羡曰：「善。

translations.literal: Xian said, 'Excellent.'
translations.idiomatic: 'Well said,' Xian agreed.

sentences.zh: 」乃舉長沙及旁三郡以拒表，遣使詣太祖。

translations.literal: Thereupon he raised Changsha and the three neighboring commanderies to resist Biao and sent envoys to the Grand Progenitor.
translations.idiomatic: He then mobilized Changsha and three adjacent commanderies against Liu Biao and dispatched messengers to the Grand Progenitor.

sentences.zh: 太祖大悦。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Progenitor was delighted.

sentences.zh: 會紹與太祖連戰，軍未得南。

translations.literal: It happened that Shao and the Grand Progenitor fought successive battles, so the army could not yet march south.
translations.idiomatic: But Shao and the Grand Progenitor were locked in repeated combat, and no southern expedition could be spared.

sentences.zh: 而表急攻羡，羡病死。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Biao pressed the attack on Xian with urgency, and Xian died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Biao meanwhile hammered Xian's positions until Xian succumbed to illness.

sentences.zh: 城陷，階遂自匿。

translations.literal: The city fell, and Jie thereupon hid himself.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, Jie went into hiding.

sentences.zh: 久之，劉表辟爲從事祭酒，欲妻以妻妹蔡氏。

translations.literal: After a long while Liu Biao summoned him as libationer-adjutant and wished to give him his younger sister by marriage, a lady of the Cai clan, as wife.
translations.idiomatic: Eventually Liu Biao appointed him libationer-adjutant and offered him his wife's younger sister from the Cai family in marriage.

sentences.zh: 階自陳已結婚，拒而不受，因辭疾告退。

translations.literal: Jie declared that he was already married, refused to accept, and on that pretext pleaded illness and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Jie stated that he was already wed, declined the match, and retired on the excuse of illness.

sentences.zh: 太祖定荆州，聞其爲張羡謀也，異之，辟爲丞相掾主簿，遷趙郡太守。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor pacified Jing Province and learned that he had devised plans for Zhang Xian, he marveled at him, summoned him as senior clerk to the chancellor's chief of staff, and promoted him to grand warden of Zhao commandery.
translations.idiomatic: After the Grand Progenitor settled Jingzhou and heard that Jie had plotted for Zhang Xian, he was struck with admiration, appointed him senior clerk to the chancellor's chief of staff, and soon advanced him to grand warden of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 魏國初建，爲虎賁中郎將侍中。

translations.literal: When the state of Wei was first founded he became commandant of the household rapid as tiger and palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of the state of Wei he was named commandant of the household rapid as tiger and palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 時太子未定，而臨菑侯植有寵。

translations.literal: At that time the heir apparent had not yet been settled, while the Marquis of Linzi, Zhi, enjoyed special favor.
translations.idiomatic: The heir had still not been chosen, while the Marquis of Linzi, Cao Zhi, basked in imperial favor.

sentences.zh: 階數陳文帝德優齒長，宜爲儲副，公規密諫，前後懇至。

translations.literal: Jie repeatedly declared that the virtues of the eventual Emperor Wen and his seniority in age made him fit to be the reserve heir; he remonstrated with the duke in private, earnestly and at length.
translations.idiomatic: Jie repeatedly argued that the future Emperor Wen's moral stature and senior birth suited him for the succession; time and again he pressed these pleas in confidential audience with the duke.

sentences.zh: 〈魏书称阶谏曰：“今太子仁冠群子，名昭海内，仁圣达节，天下莫不闻；

translations.literal: The Book of Wei records Jie's remonstrance: 'Today the heir apparent's benevolence crowns all your sons, his name resounds within the seas, he is humane, sagely, and understands proper measure, and there is none under Heaven who has not heard of it;
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Wei quotes his admonition: 'The heir's humanity surpasses every other son, his reputation fills the realm, he combines benevolence, sagacity, and measured judgment, and the empire has taken notice;'

sentences.zh: 而大王甫以植而问臣，臣诚惑之。

translations.literal: yet you have only just asked me, my lord, because of Zhi—truly I am perplexed.'
translations.idiomatic: yet you have suddenly questioned me, my lord, on account of Zhi—I confess I am bewildered.'

sentences.zh: ”於是太祖知阶笃於守正，深益重焉。〉

translations.literal: Thereupon the Grand Progenitor knew that Jie was steadfast in upholding what was right and esteemed him all the more deeply.'
translations.idiomatic: From this the Grand Progenitor saw how firmly Jie held to integrity and valued him the more deeply.'

sentences.zh: 又毛玠、徐奕以剛蹇少黨，而爲西曹掾丁儀所不善，儀屢言其短，賴階左右以自全保。

translations.literal: Moreover Mao Jie and Xu Yi, because they were stern and aloof and had few partisans, were disliked by Ding Yi, western bureau clerk; Yi repeatedly spoke of their faults, and they owed their survival to Jie's support on either side.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Jie and Xu Yi, rigid and short of allies, earned the enmity of Ding Yi, clerk of the western bureau; Yi kept denigrating them, and only Jie's steadying hand on both flanks let them escape harm.

sentences.zh: 其將順匡救，多此類也。

translations.literal: In smoothing what was compliant and remedying what was wrong, his conduct was mostly of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: Time after time he eased confrontations and righted wrongs in just this fashion.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書，典選舉。

translations.literal: He was promoted to masters of writing and placed in charge of appointments.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to masters of writing with responsibility for personnel selection.

sentences.zh: 曹仁爲關羽所圍，太祖遣徐晃救之，不解。

translations.literal: Cao Ren was besieged by Guan Yu, and the Grand Progenitor sent Xu Huang to relieve him, but the siege was not broken.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Ren lay trapped by Guan Yu; the Grand Progenitor dispatched Xu Huang to rescue him, yet the encirclement held.

sentences.zh: 太祖欲自南征，以问羣下。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor wished to lead a southern campaign in person and consulted his ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Progenitor considered marching south himself and asked his advisers.

sentences.zh: 羣下皆謂：「王不亟行，今敗矣。

translations.literal: They all said, 'If you do not go at once, my lord, we are defeated today.'
translations.idiomatic: The assembly insisted, 'Unless you ride south immediately, my lord, all is lost.'

sentences.zh: 」階獨曰：「大王以仁等爲足以料事勢不也？

translations.literal: Jie alone said, 'Does the great king believe that Ren and the others are able to read the situation or not?'
translations.idiomatic: Jie alone asked, 'Does Your Majesty credit Ren and his officers with sound judgment of the field?'

translations.literal: The reply was, 'They can.'
translations.idiomatic: The answer came: 'They can.'

sentences.zh: 」「大王恐二人遺力邪？

translations.literal: He said again, 'Does the great king fear that the two of them will hold back their strength?'
translations.idiomatic: Jie pressed, 'Do you fear they will stint their effort?'

translations.literal: The answer was, 'No.'
translations.idiomatic: 'No,' came the reply.

sentences.zh: 」「然則何爲自往？

translations.literal: He said, 'Then why go yourself?'
translations.idiomatic: Jie continued, 'Then why must you go in person?'

sentences.zh: 」曰：「吾恐虏众多，而晃等勢不便耳。

translations.literal: The answer was, 'I fear the enemy are too many and that Huang and the others are at a disadvantage.'
translations.idiomatic: 'Because I worry the bandits are too numerous and Huang's men are at a disadvantage,' was the answer.

sentences.zh: 」階曰：「今仁等处重圍之中而守死无贰者，诚以大王遠爲之勢也。

translations.literal: Jie said, 'Now Ren and the others stand in the depths of a tight siege yet hold to death without wavering because they truly rely on your distant presence as their backing.
translations.idiomatic: Jie said, 'Ren and his commanders endure a ring of steel yet cling to death without second thoughts because they trust Your Majesty's distant mass as their shield.'

sentences.zh: 夫居万死之地，必有死争之心；

translations.literal: Those who dwell in the place of ten thousand deaths are sure to harbor the will to fight to the death;
translations.idiomatic: Men pinned in a kill-box will fight as if they had nothing left to lose;

sentences.zh: 内怀死争，外有强救，大王案六軍以示餘力，何忧於敗而欲自往？

translations.literal: with the will to fight to the death within and a strong relief force without, if the great king holds the six armies in readiness to show surplus strength, why worry about defeat and wish to go yourself?'
translations.idiomatic: with that resolve inside and powerful rescue outside, if Your Majesty merely arrays the six hosts to show you still have reserves, what need is there to dread defeat or to take the field yourself?'

sentences.zh: 」太祖善其言，驻軍於摩陂。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor approved his words and halted the army at Mopo.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Progenitor accepted this counsel and encamped his army at Mopo.

sentences.zh: 贼遂退。

translations.literal: The bandits thereupon withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy then drew off.

sentences.zh: 文帝践阼，遷尚書令，封高鄉亭侯，加侍中。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen ascended the throne Jie was promoted to director of the Masters of Writing, enfeoffed as village marquis of Gaoxiang, and given additional rank as palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen took the throne, Jie became director of the Masters of Writing, was enfeoffed village marquis of Gaoxiang, and received the added title of palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 階疾病，帝自臨省，謂曰：「吾方讬六尺之孤，寄天下之命於卿。

translations.literal: Jie fell ill, and the emperor came in person to visit him, saying, 'I am about to entrust the orphan of six feet and place the fate of the realm upon you.
translations.idiomatic: Jie sickened, and the emperor visited him at bedside, saying, 'I mean to commit my six-foot heir and the destiny of the empire to you.'

sentences.zh: 勉之！

translations.literal: Strive on!'
translations.idiomatic: Do not fail me!'

sentences.zh: 」徙封安乐鄉侯，邑六百户，又赐階三子爵關内侯，祐以嗣子不封，病卒，又追赠關内侯。

translations.literal: His fief was shifted to village marquis of Anle with six hundred households; in addition the emperor bestowed on three of Jie's sons the rank of secondary marquis within the passes; You, because he was the heir, was not enfeoffed, but when he died of illness he too was posthumously awarded secondary marquis within the passes.
translations.idiomatic: His patent was moved to village marquis of Anle at six hundred households, and three of Jie's sons were each granted secondary marquis within the passes; You, as designated successor, had gone without a separate fief, yet after he died of illness he likewise received a posthumous patent as secondary marquis within the passes.

sentences.zh: 後階疾笃，遣使者即拜太常，薨，帝爲之流涕，谥曰贞侯。

translations.literal: Later, when Jie's illness grew grave, the emperor sent envoys to appoint him grand master of ceremonies on the spot; when he died the emperor wept for him and gave the posthumous title marquis Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: When Jie later sank toward death, messengers were rushed to invest him as grand master of ceremonies; at his passing the emperor shed tears and canonized him as Marquis Zhen.

sentences.zh: 子嘉嗣。

translations.literal: His son Jia succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jia inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 以階弟纂爲散骑侍郎，赐爵關内侯。

translations.literal: Jie's younger brother Zuan was appointed cavalier attendant-in-ordinary and granted secondary marquis within the passes.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor named Jie's younger brother Zuan cavalier attendant-in-ordinary and awarded him secondary marquis within the passes.

sentences.zh: 嘉尚升遷亭公主，會嘉平中，以乐安太守與吴戰於东關，軍敗，没，谥曰壮侯。

translations.literal: Jia married the princess of the Shengqian village estate; during the Jiaping era, while serving as grand warden of Le'an, he fought Wu at Dongguan, was defeated, perished, and received the posthumous title marquis Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Jia took the princess of the Shengqian village fief; in the Jiaping years, as grand warden of Le'an, he clashed with Wu at Dongguan, his army was routed, he fell in battle, and was posthumously honored as Marquis Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 子翊嗣。

translations.literal: His son Yi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yi inherited the line.

sentences.zh: 〈世说曰：阶孙陵，字元徽，有名於晋武帝世，至荥阳太守，卒。〉

translations.literal: A Shishuo entry states: Jie's grandson Ling, courtesy name Yuanhui, was famous in Emperor Wu of Jin's reign, rose to grand warden of Xingyang, and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: The Shishuo relates that Jie's grandson Ling, style Yuanhui, won renown under Jin Emperor Wu, served as grand warden of Xingyang, and died in that post.

sentences.zh: 陳羣字長文，颍川许昌

translations.literal: Chen Qun, courtesy name Zhangwen, was from Xuchang in Yingchuan
translations.idiomatic: Chen Qun, whose courtesy name was Zhangwen, hailed from Xuchang in Yingchuan

translations.literal: (a man)
translations.idiomatic: (of that commandery)

sentences.zh: 也。
祖父寔，父纪，叔父谌，皆有盛名。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shi, his father Ji, and his uncle Chen all enjoyed great renown.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shi, his father Ji, and his uncle Chen each carried towering reputations.

sentences.zh: 〈寔字仲弓、纪字元方，谌字季方。

translations.literal: Shi was styled Zhonggong, Ji Yuangfang, and Chen Jifang.
translations.idiomatic: Shi bore the style Zhonggong, Ji the style Yuangfang, and Chen the style Jifang.

sentences.zh: 《魏书》曰：寔德冠当时，纪、谌并名重於世。

translations.literal: The Book of Wei states: Shi's virtue crowned his age, while Ji and Chen were both weighty names in the world.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Wei notes that Shi's virtue outshone his contemporaries and that Ji and Chen were celebrated figures of their day.

sentences.zh: 寔为太丘长，遭党锢，隐居荆山，远近宗师之。

translations.literal: Shi became magistrate of Taiqiu; when the partisan prohibitions struck he retired to Mount Jing and was honored as teacher by those near and far.
translations.idiomatic: Shi served as magistrate of Taiqiu; when the partisan proscriptions fell he withdrew to Mount Jing, where scholars from every quarter revered him as their master.

sentences.zh: 灵帝崩，何进辅政，引用天下名士，徵寔，欲以为参军，以老病，遂不屈节，谌为司空掾，早卒。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ling died He Jin assisted the government, summoning famous men of the empire; he called for Shi to be army adviser, but Shi, citing old age and illness, refused to bend his principles; Chen became clerk to the minister of works and died young.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Ling's death He Jin directed the regency and recruited eminent scholars across the land; he summoned Shi as army adviser, but Shi pleaded age and infirmity and would not compromise his integrity; Chen took office as clerk to the minister of works and died in youth.

sentences.zh: 纪历位平原相、侍中、大鸿胪，著书数十篇，世谓之陈子。

translations.literal: Ji successively held the posts of minister of Pingyuan, palace attendant, and grand herald for foreign guests, and composed several tens of treatises; the age calls him Master Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Ji rose through minister of Pingyuan, palace attendant, and grand herald for foreign guests, and left behind dozens of essays that posterity knows as the writings of Master Chen.

sentences.zh: 寔之亡也，司空荀爽、太仆令韩融并制缌麻，执子孙礼。

translations.literal: When Shi died Minister of Works Xun Shuang and Director of Retainers Han Rong together observed the one-year mourning for him and performed the rites of grandchildren.
translations.idiomatic: At Shi's death Minister of Works Xun Shuang and Director of Retainers Han Rong jointly observed the one-year mourning for him as though they were his grandsons.

sentences.zh: 四方至者车数千乘，自太原郭泰等无不造门。

translations.literal: Those who came from the four quarters numbered several thousand carriages; none from as far as Taiyuan's Guo Tai failed to visit his gate.
translations.idiomatic: Carriages from every quarter lined up by the thousand; not even Guo Tai of Taiyuan omitted a call at his gate.

sentences.zh: 《傅子》曰：寔亡，天下致吊，会其葬者三万人，制缞麻者以百数。

translations.literal: The Fu Zi states: When Shi died the empire sent condolences; those who attended his burial were thirty thousand, and those who donned hemp mourning were reckoned in the hundreds.
translations.idiomatic: The Fu Zi records that at Shi's death the whole realm mourned, thirty thousand mourners thronged his funeral, and hundreds wore hemp in his honor.

sentences.zh: 先贤行状曰：大将军何进遣属吊祠，谥曰文范先生。

translations.literal: The Conduct of Worthies of Antiquity states: General-in-chief He Jin sent subordinates to offer sacrifices and gave him the posthumous title Master Wenfan.
translations.idiomatic: The Conduct of Worthies of Antiquity adds that General-in-chief He Jin dispatched aides to sacrifice at his tomb and canonized him Master Wenfan.

sentences.zh: 于时，寔、纪高名并著，而谌又配之，世号曰三君。

translations.literal: At that time Shi and Ji were equally celebrated in name, while Chen matched them; the age styled them the Three Gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: In that era Shi and Ji shared equal fame, Chen stood beside them, and contemporaries dubbed them the Three Gentlemen.

sentences.zh: 每宰府辟命，率皆同时，羔雁成群，丞掾交至。

translations.literal: Whenever a chief office issued summons, they were invariably called together; flocks of lambs and geese arrived, assistants and clerks came in relays.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever high offices issued appointments, the three were summoned as a set; gifts of lamb and goose arrived in flocks, and clerks crowded their doors.

sentences.zh: 豫州百姓皆图画寔、纪、谌之形象。〉

translations.literal: The commoners of Yu Province all painted images of Shi, Ji, and Chen.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Yu Province painted portraits of Shi, Ji, and Chen.

sentences.zh: 羣爲兒時，寔常奇異之，謂宗人父老曰：「此兒必兴吾宗。

translations.literal: When Qun was still a boy Shi often marveled at him, saying to the elders of the lineage, 'This child is sure to exalt our clan.'
translations.idiomatic: In Qun's boyhood Shi often marveled at him, telling the clan elders, 'This boy will bring glory to our house.'

sentences.zh: 」鲁國孔融高才倨傲，年在纪、羣之间，先與纪友，後與羣交，更爲纪拜，由是显名。

translations.literal: Kong Rong of Lu, gifted and arrogant, was between Ji and Qun in age; he first befriended Ji, later associated with Qun, and then bowed to Ji again, whereby Qun's name became illustrious.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Rong of Lu—brilliant and haughty—stood between Ji and Qun in years; he first befriended Ji, then grew close to Qun, and afterward bowed again to Ji, which made Qun's name resound.

sentences.zh: 劉备臨豫州，辟羣爲别驾。

translations.literal: When Liu Bei came to Yu Province he summoned Qun as chief clerk for separate carriage.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Bei assumed authority in Yu Province he appointed Qun chief clerk for separate carriage.

sentences.zh: 時陶谦病死，徐州迎备，备欲往，羣說备曰：「袁术尚强，今东，必與之争。

translations.literal: At that time Tao Qian died of illness and Xu Province welcomed Bei; Bei wished to go, and Qun urged Bei, saying, 'Yuan Shu is still strong; if you go east now you are sure to contend with him.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Qian had just died, and Xu Province invited Bei to take command; Bei meant to go east, but Qun warned him, 'Yuan Shu remains formidable; march east now and you will collide with him.'

sentences.zh: 吕布若袭將軍之後，將軍雖得徐州，事必无成。

translations.literal: If Lü Bu strikes at your rear, even should you gain Xu Province the affair will surely not succeed.'
translations.idiomatic: Should Lü Bu stab at your rear, even winning Xu Province will come to nothing.'

sentences.zh: 」备遂东，與袁术戰。

translations.literal: Bei thereupon went east and fought Yuan Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Bei went east anyway and fought Yuan Shu.

sentences.zh: 布果袭下邳，遣兵助术，大破备軍，备恨不用羣言。

translations.literal: Bu indeed raided Xiapi, sent troops to aid Shu, and smashed Bei's army in a great defeat; Bei regretted not using Qun's words.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu did strike Xiapi, sent reinforcements to Shu, and shattered Bei's host; Bei bitterly regretted ignoring Qun's counsel.

sentences.zh: 舉茂才，除柘令，不行，随纪避難徐州。

translations.literal: He was recommended as flourishing talent, appointed magistrate of Zhe, did not take office, and followed Ji in fleeing trouble to Xu Province.
translations.idiomatic: Nominated as flourishing talent and named magistrate of Zhe, he declined the post and accompanied Ji into exile in Xu Province.

sentences.zh: 属吕布破，太祖辟羣爲司空西曹掾属。

translations.literal: When Lü Bu was destroyed the Grand Progenitor summoned Qun as subordinate clerk to the western bureau of the minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: After Lü Bu's ruin the Grand Progenitor called Qun up as subordinate to the western bureau under the minister of works.

sentences.zh: 時有荐乐安王模、下邳周逵者，太祖辟之。

translations.literal: At that time someone recommended Wang Mo of Le'an and Zhou Kui of Xiapi, and the Grand Progenitor summoned them.
translations.idiomatic: Someone had recommended Wang Mo of Le'an and Zhou Kui of Xiapi, and the Grand Progenitor issued summons to both.

sentences.zh: 羣封還教，以爲模、逵秽德，终必敗，太祖不听。

translations.literal: Qun returned the order sealed, holding that Mo and Kui were men of foul virtue who would end in ruin; the Grand Progenitor did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Qun returned the commission sealed, arguing that Mo and Kui were morally tainted and bound to fall; the Grand Progenitor paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 後模、逵皆坐奸宄诛，太祖以谢羣。

translations.literal: Later Mo and Kui were both executed for villainy, and the Grand Progenitor apologized to Qun.
translations.idiomatic: Mo and Kui were later executed for corruption, and the Grand Progenitor apologized to Qun.

sentences.zh: 羣荐广陵陳矫、丹阳戴乾，太祖皆用之。

translations.literal: Qun recommended Chen Jiao of Guangling and Dai Qian of Danyang, and the Grand Progenitor employed them both.
translations.idiomatic: Qun nominated Chen Jiao of Guangling and Dai Qian of Danyang, and the Grand Progenitor took both into service.

sentences.zh: 後吴人叛，乾忠義死難，矫遂爲名臣，世以羣爲知人。

translations.literal: Later the people of Wu rebelled; Qian died loyally in the crisis, while Jiao became a famous minister; the age therefore deemed Qun a judge of men.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu's adherents later rose, Qian perished loyally in the fighting while Jiao rose to noted minister; contemporaries pronounced Qun a discerning recommender.

sentences.zh: 除萧、赞、長平令，父卒去官。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Xiao, Zan, and Changping; when his father died he left office.
translations.idiomatic: He was named magistrate of Xiao, Zan, and Changping, then resigned on his father's death.

sentences.zh: 後以司徒掾舉高第，爲治書侍御史，转参丞相軍事。

translations.literal: Later, recommended from the steward's office as high in grade, he became supervising secretary and censor, then transferred to staff the army of the chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Later, graded top among steward's clerks, he became supervising secretary and censor, then rotated onto the chancellor's military staff.

sentences.zh: 魏國既建，遷爲御史中丞。

translations.literal: When the state of Wei was established he was promoted to palace aide to the censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: After the state of Wei was founded he advanced to palace aide to the censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 時太祖议复肉刑，令曰：「安得通理君子达於古今者，使平斯事乎！

translations.literal: At that time the Grand Progenitor debated restoring the mutilating punishments, issuing an order: 'Where shall I find a gentleman of comprehensive principle, versed in ancient and modern, to settle this matter!
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Progenitor was then debating the revival of corporal mutilation and issued an edict: 'Where is the broad-minded gentleman, learned in past and present, who can settle this question for me!'

sentences.zh: 昔陳鸿胪以爲死刑有可加於仁恩者，正謂此也。

translations.literal: Long ago Minister Chen Honglu held that some capital sentences might receive added grace—he spoke precisely of this.'
translations.idiomatic: Minister Chen Honglu once argued that certain capital cases might still admit added mercy—he had exactly this in mind.'

sentences.zh: 御史中丞能申其父之论乎？

translations.literal: Can the palace aide to the censor-in-chief set forth his father's thesis?'
translations.idiomatic: Can you, as palace aide to the censor-in-chief, articulate your father's argument?'

sentences.zh: 」羣对曰：

translations.literal: Qun replied:
translations.idiomatic: Qun answered:

sentences.zh: 臣父纪以为汉除肉刑而增加笞，本兴仁恻而死者更众，所谓名轻而实重者也。

translations.literal: Your subject's father Ji believed that when Han abolished the mutilating punishments but increased the strokes of the bastinado, it began in benevolent pity yet more men died—what is called a light name but a heavy reality.
translations.idiomatic: My father Ji held that Han's abolition of corporal mutilation while raising the count of bastinado strokes began as an act of mercy yet left more men dead—the case of a merciful label masking a harsher truth.

sentences.zh: 名轻则易犯，实重则伤民。

translations.literal: When the name is light transgression is easy; when the reality is heavy the people are injured.
translations.idiomatic: A light-sounding penalty invites crime; a heavy reality wounds the common people.

sentences.zh: 书曰：‘惟敬五刑，以成三德。

translations.literal: The Documents say, 'Reverently apply the five punishments to help complete the three virtues.'
translations.idiomatic: The Documents declare, 'With awe apply the five punishments to perfect the three virtues.'

sentences.zh: ’易著劓、刖、灭趾之法，所以辅政助教，惩恶息杀也。

translations.literal: The Changes records the laws of cutting the nose, cutting the feet, and removing toes—means to assist government and instruction, punish evil, and stay killing.
translations.idiomatic: The Changes prescribes nose-cutting, foot-amputation, and toe removal as tools to aid governance and teaching, chastise wickedness, and curb bloodshed.

sentences.zh: 且杀人偿死，合於古制；

translations.literal: Moreover to kill a life in payment for a death accords with ancient regulation;
translations.idiomatic: Besides, life for life matches the old statutes;

sentences.zh: 至於伤人，或残毁其体而裁翦毛发，非其理也。

translations.literal: As for injuring people, sometimes the body is mutilated while only hair is trimmed—this is not in accord with principle.
translations.idiomatic: When the law injures a man, to mutilate his body yet merely clip his hair falls short of what justice demands.

sentences.zh: 若用古刑，使淫者下蚕室，盗者刖其足，则永无淫放穿窬之奸矣。

translations.literal: If the ancient punishments were applied, sending the lecher to the silkworm chamber and cutting off the thief's feet, then wanton license and burglary through walls would never arise.
translations.idiomatic: Restore the old sanctions—castrate the adulterer, amputate the thief's feet—and debauchery and house-breaking would disappear for good.

sentences.zh: 夫三千之属，虽未可悉复，若斯数者，时之所患，宜先施用。

translations.literal: Though the three thousand statutory items cannot all be revived, several such categories are what the age most dreads and ought to be put into practice first.
translations.idiomatic: We need not resurrect every clause of the old code, but the offenses that torment society today deserve priority.

sentences.zh: 汉律所杀殊死之罪，仁所不及也，其餘逮死者，可以刑杀。

translations.literal: The crimes under Han law that call for execution in the category of 'exceptionally capital' lie beyond the reach of mercy; for the rest who face death, mutilation may replace killing.
translations.idiomatic: Han statutes mark certain capital crimes as beyond clemency; for all other cases headed for execution, corporal punishment could substitute for the headsman's blade.

sentences.zh: 如此，则所刑之与所生足以相贸矣。

translations.literal: In this way what is spared by mutilation and what is given life would balance each other in exchange.
translations.idiomatic: Then the lives spared and the bodies marked would trade off in fair measure.

sentences.zh: 今以笞死之法易不杀之刑，是重人支体而轻人躯命也。

translations.literal: Now to replace non-lethal punishments with beating to death is to weigh men's limbs heavily and men's lives lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Swapping nonfatal penalties for death by flogging exalts the body over the life itself.

sentences.zh: 時锺繇與羣议同，王朗及议者多以爲未可行。

translations.literal: At that time Zhong Yao agreed with Qun's opinion, while Wang Lang and most participants in the debate thought it could not yet be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Yao sided with Qun; Wang Lang and the majority of the council still judged the scheme premature.

sentences.zh: 太祖深善繇、羣言，以軍事未罢，顾众议，故且寝。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor deeply approved the words of Yao and Qun, but because military operations had not ended he deferred to the assembly's views and therefore set the matter aside for the time being.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao endorsed both men heartily, yet with the war still on he bowed to wider opinion and shelved corporal mutilation.

sentences.zh: 是時，帝初莅政，羣上疏曰：

translations.literal: At this time the emperor had just taken up the reins of government, and Qun submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Early in the new reign Qun addressed the throne:

sentences.zh: 诗称‘仪刑文王，万邦作孚’；

translations.literal: The Odes declare, 'Take King Wen as your pattern, and the myriad regions will trust you.'
translations.idiomatic: The Classic of Poetry says, 'Model yourself on King Wen, and every state will place its faith in you.'

sentences.zh: 又曰‘刑于寡妻，至于兄弟，以御于家邦’。

translations.literal: It also says, 'Be a model to your chief wife, extend it to your brothers, and thereby govern family and state.'
translations.idiomatic: It adds, 'Begin with moral sway over your wife, carry it to your brothers, and rule your house and realm from there.'

sentences.zh: 道自近始，而化洽於天下。

translations.literal: The Way starts from what is near, and transforming influence spreads throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Moral transformation begins at home, then suffuses the empire.

sentences.zh: 自丧乱已来，干戈未戢，百姓不识王教之本，惧其陵迟巳甚。

translations.literal: Since the time of ruin and disorder arms have not been laid away; the common people no longer grasp the root of royal instruction, and I fear decline has gone very deep.
translations.idiomatic: Through rebellion and chaos the sword has never been sheathed; the people have lost sight of what legitimate rule rests on, and I dread how far standards have slipped.

sentences.zh: 陛下当盛魏之隆，荷二祖之业，天下想望至治，唯有以崇德布化，惠恤黎庶，则兆民幸甚。

translations.literal: Your Majesty stands in the full glory of mighty Wei, bearing the legacy of the two founding ancestors; all under Heaven yearns for the highest good order—only by honoring virtue, spreading moral transformation, and showing kindness to the black-haired multitude will the myriad people be greatly blessed.
translations.idiomatic: You inherit Wei at its zenith and the mantle of both imperial forebears; the realm hungers for perfect peace—exalt virtue, broadcast humane government, and care for the common folk, and the people will count themselves fortunate indeed.

sentences.zh: 夫臣下雷同，是非相蔽，国之大患也。

translations.literal: When ministers below all chant the same tune, right and wrong obscure each other—that is a great scourge for the state.
translations.idiomatic: When the court speaks with one cowed voice, truth and falsehood blur together, and the dynasty pays the price.

sentences.zh: 若不和睦则有雠党，有雠党则毁誉无端，毁誉无端则真伪失实，不可不深防备，有以绝其源流。

translations.literal: If they are not harmonious there will be factions at enmity; with factions at enmity praise and blame lose all anchor; when praise and blame lose anchor truth and falsehood no longer match reality—this must be guarded against with the utmost care, so as to cut off the source and flow.
translations.idiomatic: Discord breeds rival cliques; rival cliques spawn reckless slander; reckless slander erases the line between fact and rumor—you must choke this evil at its spring.

sentences.zh: 太和中，曹真表欲數道伐蜀，從斜谷入。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era Cao Zhen submitted a memorial wishing to attack Shu by several routes, entering through Xie Valley.
translations.idiomatic: During Taihe, Cao Zhen proposed a multi-pronged invasion of Shu through Xie Valley.

sentences.zh: 羣以爲「太祖昔到阳平攻張鲁，多收豆麦以益軍粮，鲁未下而食犹乏。

translations.literal: Qun held that 'when the Grand Progenitor formerly reached Yangping to attack Zhang Lu, he gathered beans and wheat in great quantity to augment the army's grain, yet before Lu submitted the troops were still short of food.
translations.idiomatic: Qun objected: 'When the founder marched on Yangping against Zhang Lu, he foraged beans and wheat to fill the granaries, yet Lu still held out while the army went hungry.'

sentences.zh: 今既无所因，且斜谷阻险，難以进退，转运必见钞截，多留兵守要，則损戰士，不可不熟虑也」。

translations.literal: Now there is no such resource to draw on, and moreover Xie Valley is precipitous and hard to advance or withdraw from; transport columns are sure to be plundered and cut off—if many troops are left to guard the passes the fighting men are weakened; this cannot but be pondered with care.'
translations.idiomatic: Today we lack that windfall, and Xie Valley's cliffs make retreat as perilous as advance; convoys will be ambushed, and garrisoning the defiles in strength only bleeds the field army—think this through.'

sentences.zh: 帝從羣议。

translations.literal: The emperor followed Qun's counsel.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign accepted Qun's advice.

sentences.zh: 真复表從子午道。

translations.literal: Zhen again memorialized to advance by the Ziwu Road.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Zhen renewed his request to push through the Ziwu trail.

sentences.zh: 羣又陳其不便，并言軍事用度之计。

translations.literal: Qun again set forth the disadvantages and also spoke on the reckoning of military expenditure.
translations.idiomatic: Qun reiterated the logistical objections and laid out the cost in supplies and treasure.

sentences.zh: 诏以羣议下真，真据之遂行。

translations.literal: An edict transmitted Qun's opinion to Zhen, yet Zhen relied on his own view and proceeded.
translations.idiomatic: The court forwarded Qun's dissent to Zhen, who ignored it and marched anyway.

sentences.zh: 會霖雨积日，羣又以爲宜诏真還，帝從之。

translations.literal: It happened that unbroken rains fell for many days, and Qun again held that an edict should order Zhen to return; the emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Days of downpour followed; Qun urged a recall, and this time the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 後皇女淑薨，追封谥平原懿公主。

translations.literal: Later the imperial daughter Shu died; she was posthumously enfeoffed with the title Princess Yi of Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: When the princess named Shu died, the court posthumously titled her the Princess Yi of Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 羣上疏曰：

translations.literal: Qun submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Qun wrote again:

sentences.zh: 长短有命，存亡有分。

translations.literal: Length of life and death have their allotted span.
translations.idiomatic: Long life and early death each have their allotted measure.

sentences.zh: 故圣人制礼，或抑或致，以求厥中。

translations.literal: Therefore the sages instituted ritual, sometimes restraining and sometimes encouraging, in order to seek the mean.
translations.idiomatic: The sages framed rites that withhold or lavish mourning precisely to strike the golden mean.

sentences.zh: 防墓有不脩之俭，嬴、博有不归之魂。

translations.literal: The tomb at Fang may go untended in frugal fashion; souls at Ying and Bo need not return home.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius left his parents' graves at Fang untended in the name of simplicity; the spirit of Bo Qi never came home from Ying and Bo.

sentences.zh: 夫大人动合天地，垂之无穷，又大德不逾闲，动为师表故也。

translations.literal: Great men move in harmony with Heaven and Earth, leaving a model for endless ages, and because great virtue does not step beyond proper bounds, their actions become the teacher for all.
translations.idiomatic: A sage-king's conduct mirrors heaven and earth, endures for ages, and never oversteps moral limits, so every gesture instructs the world.

sentences.zh: 八岁下殇，礼所不备，况未期月，而以成人礼送之，加为制服，举朝素衣，朝夕哭临，自古已来，未有此比。

translations.literal: An 'early death' below eight sui is not provided for in the rites; how much less one who has not completed a full month—yet to send her off with the rites of an adult, add full mourning garments, have the whole court in undyed cloth, and wail morning and evening at her bier—since antiquity there has been no parallel.
translations.idiomatic: The canon omits funeral rites for children who die before eight; for an infant not yet a month old to receive an adult obsequy, full mourning dress, court-wide hemp, and daily keening has no precedent in history.

sentences.zh: 而乃复自往视陵，亲临祖载。

translations.literal: Yet you again go in person to view the mausoleum and attend the sending-off.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Your Majesty means to visit the tomb yourself and preside at the hearse.

sentences.zh: 原陛下抑割无益有损之事，但悉听群臣送葬，乞车驾不行，此万国之至望也。

translations.literal: I beg Your Majesty to restrain and set aside what brings no benefit but harm, and simply let the ministers conduct the burial, asking that the imperial carriage not go forth—this is the utmost hope of the myriad states.
translations.idiomatic: Suppress the needless journey, let the officials bury her, and keep the chariot at home—that is what every principality prays for.

sentences.zh: 闻车驾欲幸摩陂，实到许昌，二宫上下，皆悉俱东，举朝大小，莫不惊怪。

translations.literal: I have heard that the imperial train intends to visit Mopo but will in fact reach Xuchang; both palaces, high and low, are all to move east, and every rank in court is startled and perplexed.
translations.idiomatic: Word says you will travel to Mobo but actually halt at Xuchang; both inner and outer palaces are packing east, and the whole bureaucracy is dumbfounded.

sentences.zh: 或言欲以避衰，或言欲於便处移殿舍，或不知何故。

translations.literal: Some say it is to flee ill omens, some say to shift the halls to a convenient site, some do not know the reason.
translations.idiomatic: Some whisper you flee a curse, some that you mean to relocate the halls, some admit they cannot guess.

sentences.zh: 臣以为吉凶有命，祸福由人，移徙求安，则亦无益。

translations.literal: Your subject believes fortune and misfortune have their fate, weal and woe come from human conduct; to move dwelling seeking safety brings no real gain.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that luck is heaven's decree but conduct shapes disaster; flitting about for safety avails nothing.

sentences.zh: 若必当移避，缮治金墉城西宫，及孟津别宫，皆可权时分止。

translations.literal: If a move is truly unavoidable, repair the western palace at Jinyong fortress or the separate palace at Mengjin—either can serve for a temporary halt.
translations.idiomatic: If flight is unavoidable, refurbish the western compound at Jinyong or the detached palace at Mengjin—either will do for a short stay.

sentences.zh: 可无举宫暴露野次，废损盛节蚕农之要。

translations.literal: There is no need to expose the entire palace in the open wilds, wasting the great seasonal work of silkworms and farming.
translations.idiomatic: Do not drag the whole household into the open, wrecking the spring silkworm season and the plough.

sentences.zh: 又贼地闻之，以为大衰。

translations.literal: Moreover when the enemy hear of it they will take it for a great portent of doom.
translations.idiomatic: Enemy spies will read such a stampede as a sign of Wei in collapse.

sentences.zh: 加所烦费，不可计量。

translations.literal: Added to the bother, the expense cannot be reckoned.
translations.idiomatic: The cost, piled on the confusion, staggers reckoning.

sentences.zh: 且

translations.literal: Moreover
translations.idiomatic: Moreover

translations.literal: (from)
translations.idiomatic: (from)

sentences.zh: 吉士贤人，当盛衰，处安危，秉道信命，非徙其家以宁，乡邑从其风化，无恐惧之心。

translations.literal: worthy gentlemen and good men, when they meet prosperity or decline, stand in safety or peril, uphold the Way and trust fate—not only does their own household thereby find peace, but town and village follow their transforming influence without hearts of fear.
translations.idiomatic: The noble man, in boom or bust, cleaves to principle and accepts heaven's lot; his family rests easy, his neighbors take heart from his example, and fear leaves them.

sentences.zh: 况乃帝王万国之主，静则天下安，动则天下扰；

translations.literal: How much more the Son of Heaven, lord of the myriad regions—when he is still the realm is calm, when he stirs the realm is disturbed;
translations.idiomatic: Far more the emperor, master of all lands: his stillness steadies the world, his restlessness shakes it;

sentences.zh: 行止动静，岂可轻脱哉？

translations.literal: can his comings and goings be treated lightly?'
translations.idiomatic: can his movements be trifled with?'

sentences.zh: 帝不听。

translations.literal: The emperor did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign brushed the plea aside.

sentences.zh: 青龙中，营治宫室，百姓失农時。

translations.literal: In the Qinglong era palace chambers were built and the people missed the farming season.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qinglong, palace construction pulled peasants from the fields at sowing time.

sentences.zh: 羣上疏曰：

translations.literal: Qun submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Qun memorialized:

sentences.zh: 禹承唐、虞之盛，犹卑宫室而恶衣服，况今丧乱之后，人民至少，比汉文、景之时，不过一大郡。

translations.literal: Yu inherited the splendor of Tang and Shun, yet still dwelt in lowly halls and wore coarse garments; how much more after the age of ruin and disorder, when the people are very few—not equal even to a single large commandery in the time of Han Wendi and Jingdi.
translations.idiomatic: Great Yu took over a golden age yet kept humble roofs and rough clothes; after our wars the population is thinner than a single populous commandery under Wen and Jing of Han.

sentences.zh: 〈臣松之案：《汉书地理志》云：元始二年，天下户口最盛，汝南郡为大郡，有三十餘万户。

translations.literal: Pei Songzhi notes: The 'Treatise on Geography' in the Han History states that in the second year of Yuanshi, when household registers peaked, Runan commandery, the largest, had somewhat more than three hundred thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Songzhi comments: the Han Geography monograph records that at the Yuanshi zenith Runan, the biggest commandery, held a little over three hundred thousand households.

sentences.zh: 则文、景之时不能如是多也。

translations.literal: Thus in the time of Wen and Jing the numbers could not have been so great.
translations.idiomatic: Wen and Jing's era could not have matched that census.

sentences.zh: 案《晋太康三年地记》，晋户有三百七十七万，吴、蜀户不能居半。

translations.literal: According to the 'Jin Geography of the third year of Taikang,' Jin had 3,770,000 households, and Wu and Shu together did not reach half.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin land register for Taikang 3 lists 3.77 million households under Jin, with Wu and Shu combined still short of half that.

sentences.zh: 以此言之，魏虽始承丧乱，方晋亦当无乃大殊。

translations.literal: Judging by this, although Wei first inherited ruin and disorder, compared with Jin the difference ought not to be enormous.
translations.idiomatic: Wei began amid rubble, yet its head count cannot have diverged wildly from Jin's.

sentences.zh: 长文之言，於是为过。〉

translations.literal: Zhangwen's words are therefore exaggerated.'
translations.idiomatic: Zhangwen's comparison overshoots the mark.'

sentences.zh: 加边境有事，将士劳苦，若有水旱之患，国家之深忧也。

translations.literal: Add to this trouble on the borders, toil for officers and men, and if flood or drought should strike, that is the state's deepest worry.
translations.idiomatic: Layer on frontier alarms, weary troops, and a drought or flood becomes a nightmare.

sentences.zh: 且吴、蜀未灭，社稷不安。

translations.literal: Moreover Wu and Shu are not yet destroyed and the altars of soil and grain are not secure.
translations.idiomatic: Wu and Shu still stand; the dynasty is not safe.

sentences.zh: 宜及其未动，讲武劝农，有以待之。

translations.literal: It is fitting, before they stir, to drill the army and encourage farming so as to be prepared.
translations.idiomatic: Train the hosts and push the plough before those foes move.

sentences.zh: 今舍此急而先宫室，臣惧百姓遂困，将何以应敌？

translations.literal: Now to set aside this urgency and put palaces first—I fear the people will sink into distress; with what shall we answer the enemy?'
translations.idiomatic: To postpone that work for marble halls is to beggar the people—how then do we meet the foe?'

sentences.zh: 昔刘备自成都至白水，多作传舍，兴费人役，太祖知其疲民也。

translations.literal: Long ago Liu Bei, from Chengdu to Baishui, built many relay stations, raising expense and corvée labor; the Grand Progenitor knew he was exhausting the people.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei once lined the road from Chengdu to Baishui with post-houses, bleeding labor and coin—Cao Cao read that as self-strangulation.

sentences.zh: 今中国劳力，亦吴、蜀之所原。

translations.literal: Now the Central Plain strains its labor—this is exactly what Wu and Shu desire.
translations.idiomatic: Driving China to exhaustion is precisely what our rivals hope for.

sentences.zh: 此安危之机也，惟陛下虑之。

translations.literal: This is the pivot of safety and peril; I beg Your Majesty to ponder it.
translations.idiomatic: Here hangs victory or ruin; weigh it carefully.

sentences.zh: 帝答曰：「王者宫室，亦宜并立。

translations.literal: The emperor replied, 'A king's palaces ought also to be established in parallel.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor answered, 'A Son of Heaven needs fitting halls beside his other duties.'

sentences.zh: 灭贼之後，但当罢守耳，岂可复兴役邪？

translations.literal: After the bandits are destroyed we need only dismantle the garrisons—how could corvée be raised again?'
translations.idiomatic: Once the rebels fall we will only disband excess troops—why fear new levies?'

sentences.zh: 是故君之职，萧何之大略也。

translations.literal: Therefore this is the ruler's charge—the broad plan of Xiao He.'
translations.idiomatic: That is a ruler's burden—the lesson Xiao He taught.'

sentences.zh: 」羣又曰：

translations.literal: Qun said again:
translations.idiomatic: Qun pressed on:

sentences.zh: 昔汉祖唯与项羽争天下，羽已灭，宫室烧焚，是以萧何建武库、太仓，皆是要急，然犹非其壮丽。

translations.literal: Long ago Han Gaozu contended with Xiang Yu alone for the realm; when Yu was destroyed the palaces were burned, and therefore Xiao He built the armory and the grand granary—all were urgent needs—yet even these were not made magnificent.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu fought only Xiang Yu; when Chu fell the Chang'an palaces were ash, so Xiao He threw up arsenals and granaries—utter necessities—yet even those stayed plain.

sentences.zh: 今二虏未平，诚不宜与古同也。

translations.literal: Now the two foes are not yet pacified—it is truly not fitting to match antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: With two enemies still in the field, aping the ancients is unwise.

sentences.zh: 〈孙盛曰：周礼，天子之宫，有斫蹐之制。

translations.literal: Sun Sheng says: In the Rites of Zhou the Son of Heaven's palace had regulations for carved steps.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng notes that Zhou ritual prescribed even the king's stair treads.

sentences.zh: 然质文之饰，与时推移。

translations.literal: Yet the adornment of substance versus pattern shifts with the times.
translations.idiomatic: Ornament and simplicity shift with each age.

sentences.zh: 汉承周、秦之弊，宜敦简约之化，而何崇饰宫室，示侈后嗣。

translations.literal: Han inherited the faults of Zhou and Qin and ought to promote a culture of austerity, yet why did he glorify palace chambers and display extravagance to later heirs?
translations.idiomatic: Han took Zhou and Qin's excesses and should have preached frugality—why instead parade palace splendor for posterity?

sentences.zh: 此乃武帝千门万户所以大兴，岂无所复增之谓邪？

translations.literal: This is why Emperor Wu opened his thousand gates and myriad doors in such grand construction—can it mean there was nothing further to add?'
translations.idiomatic: That is how Han Wudi came to multiply gates and halls without end—was there truly nothing left to build?'

sentences.zh: 况乃魏氏方有吴、蜀之难，四海罹涂炭之艰，而述萧何之过议，以为令轨，岂不惑於大道而昧得失之辨哉？

translations.literal: How much more when the house of Wei still faces the hardship of Wu and Shu and the four seas suffer the scourge of mud and charcoal—yet one rehearses Xiao He's faulted counsel and calls it a model—can this be anything but confusion about the great Way and blindness to gain and loss?'
translations.idiomatic: Wei still bleeds against Wu and Shu while the empire smolders—yet we cite Xiao He's mistake as precedent. Is that not a muddle of the Way itself?'

sentences.zh: 使百代之君，眩於奢俭之中，何之由矣。

translations.literal: If rulers through a hundred generations are dazzled between extravagance and austerity, by what path shall they find the right course?'
translations.idiomatic: If every future throne wavers between luxury and stinginess, where lies the middle road?'

sentences.zh: 诗云：“斯言之玷，不可为也。

translations.literal: The Odes says, 'The flaw in these words cannot be undone.'
translations.idiomatic: The Poetry warns, 'A slip of the tongue cannot be repaired.'

sentences.zh: ”其斯之谓乎！〉

translations.literal: Does it not speak of this!'
translations.idiomatic: Does it not mean exactly this!'

sentences.zh: 夫人之所欲，莫不有辞，况乃天王，莫之敢违。

translations.literal: What men desire they always have words to excuse; how much more the heavenly king—none dares oppose him.
translations.idiomatic: Mortals rationalize every appetite; the August One faces no veto.

sentences.zh: 前欲坏武库，谓不可不坏也；

translations.literal: Earlier you wished to demolish the armory, saying it could not but be torn down;
translations.idiomatic: First you ordered the arsenal razed as unavoidable;

sentences.zh: 后欲置之，谓不可不置也。

translations.literal: later you wished to set it up again, saying it could not but be established.
translations.idiomatic: then you ordered it rebuilt as equally unavoidable.

sentences.zh: 若必作之，固非臣下辞言所屈；

translations.literal: If you insist on building, it is truly not something ministerial words can bend;
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty insists, no memorial can deflect you;

sentences.zh: 若少留神，卓然回意，亦非臣下之所及也。

translations.literal: yet if you would pause a moment and suddenly turn your intention, that too lies beyond what ministers can achieve.
translations.idiomatic: yet a moment's reflection and a change of heart are likewise beyond our power to command.

sentences.zh: 汉明帝欲起德阳殿，锺离意谏，即用其言，后乃复作之；

translations.literal: Emperor Ming of Han wished to raise the Deyang Hall; Zhong Li Yi remonstrated, and the emperor immediately used his words, yet later built it again;
translations.idiomatic: Han Mingdi planned the Deyang Palace; Zhong Li Yi protested, and the emperor yielded—only to resume construction later;

sentences.zh: 殿成，谓群臣曰：‘锺离尚书在，不得成此殿也。

translations.literal: when the hall was completed he said to the assembly, 'If Director Zhong Li of the Masters of Writing were still here, this hall could not have been finished.'
translations.idiomatic: at the dedication he told his court, 'Had Director Zhong Li lived, this hall would never have risen.'

sentences.zh: ’夫王者岂惮一臣，盖为百姓也。

translations.literal: A king ought not to fear a single minister—he acts for the sake of the common people.
translations.idiomatic: A king does not dread one upright official; he thinks of the multitude.

sentences.zh: 今臣曾不能少凝圣听，不及意远矣。

translations.literal: Now your subject has been unable even slightly to fix Your Majesty's hearing—I fall far short of Yi.
translations.idiomatic: I have failed to fix your ear as Zhong Li did—I am no match for that man.

sentences.zh: 帝於是有所减省。

translations.literal: Thereupon the emperor somewhat reduced and curtailed the project.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor trimmed the project somewhat.

sentences.zh: 初，太祖時，劉廙坐弟與魏讽謀反，当诛。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the time of the Grand Progenitor, Liu Yi sat because his younger brother plotted rebellion with Wei Feng and was liable to execution.
translations.idiomatic: Under the founder, Liu Yi was implicated when his brother joined Wei Feng's plot and faced death.

sentences.zh: 羣言之太祖，太祖曰：「廙，名臣也，吾亦欲赦之。

translations.literal: Qun spoke of him to the Grand Progenitor, and the Grand Progenitor said, 'Yi is a famous minister; I too wish to pardon him.'
translations.idiomatic: Qun interceded; Cao Cao replied, 'Yi is a noted servant of the state—I mean to spare him.'

sentences.zh: 」乃复位。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yi was restored to office.
translations.idiomatic: The court reinstated Yi in his post.

sentences.zh: 廙深德羣，羣曰：「夫议刑爲國，非爲私也；

translations.literal: Yi deeply thanked Qun, and Qun said, 'Deliberating punishments is for the state, not for private ends;
translations.idiomatic: Yi overwhelmed Qun with gratitude; Qun answered, 'Law exists for the realm, not for private debts;'

sentences.zh: 且自明主之意，吾何知焉？

translations.literal: moreover it was the intention of an enlightened ruler—what did I know of it?'
translations.idiomatic: besides, the decision was the enlightened ruler's—what part was mine?'

sentences.zh: 」其弘博不伐，皆此類也。

translations.literal: His breadth and refusal to boast were mostly of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: Such magnanimity without self-praise typified him.

sentences.zh: 青龙四年薨，谥曰靖侯。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Qinglong he died and received the posthumous title Marquis Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Qinglong 4 and was canonized Marquis Jing.

sentences.zh: 子泰嗣。

translations.literal: His son Tai succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Tai inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 帝追思羣功德，分羣户邑，封一子列侯。

translations.literal: The emperor recalled Qun's merit and virtue, divided Qun's fief households, and enfeoffed one son as full marquis.
translations.idiomatic: The court remembered his service, split his tax households, and raised one son to full marquis.

sentences.zh: 〈魏书曰：群前后数密陈得失，每上封事，辄削其草，时人及其子弟莫能知也。

translations.literal: The Book of Wei states: Qun several times secretly set forth gains and losses; whenever he submitted a sealed memorial he scraped away the draft, so that people of the time and even his sons and nephews could not know.
translations.idiomatic: Wei records that Qun often sent confidential critiques, then erased every draft so contemporaries and kin never saw his words.

sentences.zh: 论者或讥群居位拱默，正始中诏撰群臣上书，以为名臣奏议，朝士乃见群谏事，皆叹息焉。

translations.literal: Critics sometimes ridiculed Qun for occupying high office yet folding his hands in silence; in the Zhengshi era an edict ordered compilation of ministers' memorials into 'Memorials of Famous Ministers,' and only then did courtiers see Qun's remonstrances and all sighed.
translations.idiomatic: Detractors called him a silent placeholder; when Zhengshi editors gathered famous memorials, the court discovered his stack of suppressed advice and marveled.

sentences.zh: 袁子曰：或云“故少府杨阜岂非忠臣哉？

translations.literal: Master Yuan says: Someone asked, 'Was not Yang Fu, former minister of the household, a loyal minister?
translations.idiomatic: Yuan's essay asks: 'Was Yang Fu of the household not loyal?'

sentences.zh: 见人主之非，则勃然怒而触之，与人言未尝不道也，岂非所谓‘王臣謇謇，匪躬之故’者欤！

translations.literal: When he saw the ruler's faults he flared with anger and struck at them; in speaking with others he never failed to mention them—is this not what is called, 'The king's minister, stern and unbending, not for his body's sake'?'
translations.idiomatic: He thundered at every imperial error and repeated each to everyone he met—is that not the classic 'unbending servant who risks his skin for duty'?'

sentences.zh: ”答曰：“然可谓直士，忠则吾不知也。

translations.literal: The answer was, 'He may be called a blunt man; as for loyalty, I do not know.'
translations.idiomatic: The reply runs, 'Call him blunt if you like; loyal is another question.'

sentences.zh: 夫仁者爱人。

translations.literal: The humane man loves others.
translations.idiomatic: The humane man cherishes his fellow men.

sentences.zh: 施於君谓之忠，施於亲谓之孝。

translations.literal: Applied to the ruler it is called loyalty; applied to parents it is called filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: What you owe the sovereign is named loyalty; what you owe your parents is named filial duty.

sentences.zh: 忠孝者，其本一也。

translations.literal: Loyalty and filial piety share the same root.
translations.idiomatic: At bottom, loyalty to the throne and love of parents are one virtue.

sentences.zh: 故仁爱之至者，君亲有过，谏而不入，求之反覆，不得已而言，不忍宣也。

translations.literal: Therefore when benevolent love reaches its height, if lord or parent errs and remonstrance does not enter, one presses again and again until, having no choice, one speaks—yet still cannot bear to broadcast the fault.
translations.idiomatic: The truly humane, finding a flaw in ruler or father that counsel cannot mend, will argue the point repeatedly and only at the last speak out—never airing the shame in public.

sentences.zh: 今为人臣，见人主失道，直诋其非而播扬其恶，可谓直士，未为忠臣也。

translations.literal: Now, as a subject, to see the sovereign stray from the Way, bluntly revile his mistakes, and trumpet his shame may earn the name of blunt man; it does not yet make a loyal minister.
translations.idiomatic: A courtier who spots the throne's folly and shouts it abroad may pass for blunt; he has not yet earned the title of loyal.

sentences.zh: 故司空陈群则不然，其谈论终日，未尝言人主之非；

translations.literal: Thus Minister of Works Chen Qun was not so: through a whole day's talk he never uttered the ruler's faults;
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Chen Qun took a different path—hours of discourse without a word against his lord;

sentences.zh: 书数十上而外人不知。

translations.literal: he submitted dozens of sealed memorials while outsiders knew nothing.
translations.idiomatic: yet he filed score on score of palace memorials that no outsider ever saw.

sentences.zh: 君子谓群於是乎长者矣。

translations.literal: The gentleman pronounces Qun, in this, a man of true maturity.
translations.idiomatic: Men of judgment call that conduct worthy of an elder statesman.
'. (Close of the embedded essay.)

sentences.zh: 子 泰

translations.literal: Son: Tai
translations.idiomatic: His son: Chen Tai

sentences.zh: 泰字玄伯。

translations.literal: Tai, courtesy name Xuanbo.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Tai bore the courtesy name Xuanbo.

sentences.zh: 青龙中，除散骑侍郎。

translations.literal: During the Qinglong era he was appointed cavalier attendant-in-ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Qinglong reign he received appointment as cavalier attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 正始中，徙游擊將軍，爲并州刺史，加振威將軍，使持节，护匈奴中郎將，怀柔夷民，甚有威惠。

translations.literal: In the Zhengshi era he was transferred to general of agile assault, became inspector of Bing Province, was given the additional title general who rouses might, was granted the staff of authority as credential-bearing envoy, and served as colonel protecting the Xiongnu, winning over the tribes with kindness and awe.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhengshi he rotated to general of agile assault, took Bing Province as his inspectorate, added the title general who rouses might, carried the credential staff as colonel protecting the Xiongnu, and soothed the border peoples with a mix of sternness and grace.

sentences.zh: 京邑贵人多寄宝货，因泰市奴婢，泰皆挂之於壁，不发其封，及徵爲尚書，悉以還之。

translations.literal: Many grandees of the capital entrusted him with treasure to buy slaves and maidservants; Tai hung every parcel on his wall without breaking the seals, and when he was recalled as master of writing he returned them all intact.
translations.idiomatic: Capital magnates parked gold with him to purchase bond servants; he strung the sealed bundles on his wall untouched, then, on promotion to the Masters of Writing, handed every item back.

sentences.zh: 嘉平初，代郭淮爲雍州刺史，加奋威將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jiaping he replaced Guo Huai as inspector of Yong Province and was given the additional title general who displays might.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jiaping he succeeded Guo Huai in Yongzhou and added the title general who displays might.

sentences.zh: 蜀大將軍姜维率众依麹山筑二城，使牙门將句安、李歆等守之，聚羌胡质任等寇偪諸郡。

translations.literal: Shu's grand general Jiang Wei led a host to build two fortresses against Mount Qu, stationed yamen generals Gou An, Li Xin, and others to hold them, and massed Qiang and Hu hostages and raiders to press the border commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wei of Shu threw up twin strongholds on Mount Qu under commanders Gou An and Li Xin, stockpiled Qiang and Hu hostages, and harried Wei's western commanderies.

sentences.zh: 征西將軍郭淮與泰謀所以御之，泰曰：「麹城雖固，去蜀险遠，当须运粮。

translations.literal: The western expedition general Guo Huai consulted Tai on how to meet the threat; Tai said, 'Though the Qu fortresses are strong, they lie far from Shu across perilous ground and must depend on convoys for grain.
translations.idiomatic: General Guo Huai asked Tai's plan; Tai replied, 'The Qu citadels are tough, but Shu is a long march over bad roads—they live or die by supply trains.'

sentences.zh: 羌夷患维劳役，必未肯附。

translations.literal: The Qiang tribes resent Jiang Wei's corvée labor and surely will not willingly attach themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The Qiang chafe under Jiang Wei's labor levies and will not cling to him by choice.

sentences.zh: 今圍而取之，可不血刃而拔其城；

translations.literal: If we now invest and seize them, we can take the cities without drawing blood on the blades.
translations.idiomatic: Besiege them now and we may win the walls without a pitched battle.

sentences.zh: 雖其有救，山道阻险，非行兵之地也。

translations.literal: Even if relief comes, the mountain tracks are blocked and steep—not ground for marching armies.'
translations.idiomatic: Even if reinforcements arrive, those cliff roads are no place to maneuver an army.'

sentences.zh: 」淮從泰计，使泰率討蜀护軍徐质、南安太守邓艾等进兵圍之，断其运道及城外流水。

translations.literal: Huai followed Tai's plan, ordering Tai to lead Shu-conquest protector Xu Zhi, Nan'an grand warden Deng Ai, and others to advance and besiege the cities, cutting their supply lines and the streams outside the walls.
translations.idiomatic: Huai adopted the scheme: Tai advanced with protector Xu Zhi, Grand Warden Deng Ai of Nan'an, and the rest, ringed the fortresses, and severed both grain routes and the watercourses beyond the ramparts.

sentences.zh: 安等挑戰，不许，將士困窘，分粮聚雪以稽日月。

translations.literal: Gou An and others challenged to battle but were refused permission; officers and men were desperate, dividing grain and melting snow to drag out the days.
translations.idiomatic: Gou An's men shouted for a sortie and were ignored; starving, they rationed millet and scooped snow to buy time.

sentences.zh: 维果來救，出自牛头山，與泰相对。

translations.literal: Jiang Wei indeed came to the rescue, emerging from Ox Head Mountain to face Tai across the valley.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wei marched to their relief out of Ox Head Mountain and drew up opposite Tai.

sentences.zh: 泰曰：「兵法贵在不戰而屈人。

translations.literal: Tai said, 'The art of war esteems subduing the enemy without battle.
translations.idiomatic: Tai observed, 'The canon prizes breaking the foe without crossing swords.'

sentences.zh: 今绝牛头，维无反道，則我之禽也。

translations.literal: Now if we sever Ox Head Mountain, Jiang Wei has no road of return and becomes our prisoner.'
translations.idiomatic: Cut Ox Head and Jiang Wei cannot retreat—he falls into our net.'

sentences.zh: 」敕諸軍各堅垒勿與戰，遣使白淮，欲自南渡白水，循水而东，使淮趣牛头，截其還路，可并取维，不惟安等而已。

translations.literal: He ordered each army to hold its ramparts and refuse battle, sent a messenger to inform Huai, planned himself to cross the Bai River from the south and follow the stream eastward, and had Huai hurry toward Ox Head Mountain to block the line of retreat—thus Jiang Wei could be taken together with Gou An and the rest, not Gou An alone.'
translations.idiomatic: He told every column to stand fast in camp, wrote Huai to cross the Bai upstream, sweep east along the bank, and drive for Ox Head to cork Jiang Wei's escape—bagging Jiang Wei along with the garrison, not only Gou An.'

sentences.zh: 淮善其策，进率諸軍軍洮水。

translations.literal: Huai approved this strategy and advanced, leading all armies to encamp on the Tao River.
translations.idiomatic: Huai endorsed the maneuver and marched the host to the Tao.

sentences.zh: 维惧，遁走，安等孤县，遂皆降。

translations.literal: Jiang Wei grew afraid and fled; Gou An and the others, isolated, thereupon all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wei lost his nerve and bolted; Gou An's detachment, left alone, capitulated.

sentences.zh: 姜维提轻兵深入，正欲与我争锋原野，求一战之利。

translations.literal: Jiang Wei was leading light troops deep into our territory precisely to meet us on open ground and wrest a single decisive victory.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wei had plunged inland with a light column hoping to force a field battle and snatch one sharp triumph.

sentences.zh: 王经当高壁深垒，挫其锐气。

translations.literal: Wang Jing ought to have raised high walls and deep moats to blunt their edge.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jing should have locked his gates behind towering walls and drowned their momentum.

sentences.zh: 今乃与战，使贼得计，走破王经，封之狄道。

translations.literal: Instead he gave battle, letting the bandits have their way, routed Wang Jing, and besieged him in Didao.
translations.idiomatic: Instead he offered battle, played into the enemy's hands, was shattered, and was driven to shelter in Didao.

sentences.zh: 若维以战克之威，进兵东向，据栎阳积谷之实，放兵收降，招纳羌、胡，东争关、陇，传檄四郡，此我之所恶也。

translations.literal: If Jiang Wei, riding the prestige of that victory, advanced east, seized the grain stored at Liyang, released troops to gather surrendering cities, recruited Qiang and Hu, and contested Guan and Long to the east, sending proclamations through the four commanderies—that is what we would dread.
translations.idiomatic: Had Jiang Wei exploited the rout to push east, occupy Liyang's granaries, fan out to accept surrenders, enlist Qiang and Hu, and strike for the Tong Pass and Longxi, posting manifestos across the four western commanderies—that is the nightmare scenario.

sentences.zh: 而维以乘胜之兵，挫峻城之下，锐气之卒，屈力致命，攻守势殊，客主不同。

translations.literal: Yet Jiang Wei, with an army flushed by victory, now butts against steep walls; his keen soldiers exhaust their strength in a death grapple, while the forms of attack and defense differ and guest and host are not the same.
translations.idiomatic: Instead his victorious troops now hammer a sheer citadel; elite fighters spend their fury in a siege where attacker and defender face unequal odds.

sentences.zh: 兵书云‘脩橹轒榅，三月乃成，拒堙三月而后已’。

translations.literal: The military treatise says, 'To prepare mantlets and covered rams takes three months; to raise siegeworks and earthworks takes three months more.'
translations.idiomatic: The canon warns that mantlets and battering rams need three months, and siege mounds another three.

sentences.zh: 诚非轻军远入，维之诡谋仓卒所办。

translations.literal: It is truly not something a light column far from home and Jiang Wei's hasty stratagems can accomplish overnight.
translations.idiomatic: That is not work for a stripped column deep in enemy country or for Jiang Wei's improvised tricks.

sentences.zh: 县军远侨，粮谷不继，是我速进破贼之时也，所谓疾雷不及掩耳，自然之势也。

translations.literal: An isolated army, far from base, its grain not continuing—this is the moment for us to advance quickly and break the bandits; it is what is called thunder too swift for ear-covering, the tendency of nature itself.
translations.idiomatic: A lone expedition, short of provisions—that is our cue to strike fast; call it lightning too quick to clap hands over the ears.

sentences.zh: 洮水带其表，维等在其内，今乘高据势，临其项领，不战必走。

translations.literal: The Tao River girdles them without while Jiang Wei and his men are within; now if we seize the heights and hold the terrain, pressing their necks and throats, without battle they are sure to flee.
translations.idiomatic: The Tao hems them in; Jiang Wei is trapped inside. Seize the high ground, close fingers on their throat, and they flee without a fight.

sentences.zh: 寇不可纵，围不可久，君等何言如此？

translations.literal: The foe must not be indulged; a siege must not drag on—why do you speak thus?'
translations.idiomatic: Bandits cannot be pampered; a ring cannot yawn for months—why counsel delay?'

sentences.zh: 遂进軍度高城岭，潜行，夜至狄道东南高山上，多舉烽火，鸣鼓角。

translations.literal: He therefore advanced the army, crossed Gaocheng Ridge by stealth, marched by night to the high mountain southeast of Didao, raised many beacon fires, and beat drums and blew horns.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed Gaocheng Ridge unseen, climbed by night to the heights southeast of Didao, lit signal fires along the ridge, and set drums and horns roaring.

sentences.zh: 狄道城中將士见救者至，皆愤踊。

translations.literal: The officers and men inside Didao, seeing rescuers arrive, all leapt with renewed courage.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison of Didao, seeing relief appear, surged with new fight.

sentences.zh: 维始謂官救兵当须众集乃发，而卒聞已至，謂有奇变宿謀，上下震惧。

translations.literal: Jiang Wei had at first supposed government relief must wait until forces massed before setting out, but suddenly hearing they had already arrived, thought some strange stratagem lay behind it; high and low were shaken with fear.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wei had assumed Wei would mass a huge host before moving; hearing troops already on the ridge, he suspected sorcery or a long-laid ambush, and panic rippled through his ranks.

sentences.zh: 自軍之发陇西也，以山道深险，贼必设伏。

translations.literal: From the time the army set out from Longxi, because the mountain roads were deep and perilous, the bandits were sure to lay ambushes.
translations.idiomatic: Since leaving Longxi Tai had reckoned the enemy would plant ambushes along the defiles.

sentences.zh: 泰诡從南道，维果三日施伏。

translations.literal: Tai feigned a march on the southern road, and Jiang Wei indeed spent three days laying ambushes.
translations.idiomatic: He feinted along the southern track while Jiang Wei wasted three days setting traps.

sentences.zh: 〈臣松之案：此传云“谓救兵当须众集，而卒闻已至，谓有奇变，上下震惧”，此则救至出於不意。

translations.literal: Pei Songzhi notes: This biography says 'they thought relief must wait until forces assembled, yet suddenly heard it had arrived and supposed some strange change—high and low were terrified,' which implies the rescue came unexpectedly.
translations.idiomatic: Songzhi observes: the text says the Shu army expected a delayed muster yet was startled by an immediate arrival—implying surprise.

sentences.zh: 若不知救至，何故伏兵深险乃经三日乎？

translations.literal: If they did not know relief had come, why would they lay ambushes in the deep defiles for three full days?
translations.idiomatic: Had they not anticipated relief, why spend three days mining the passes?

sentences.zh: 设伏相伺，非不知之谓。

translations.literal: To set ambush and watch for the enemy is not the same as not knowing.'
translations.idiomatic: Lying in wait is the opposite of ignorance.'

sentences.zh: 此皆语之不通也。〉

translations.literal: This is all incoherent language.'〉
translations.idiomatic: The whole passage contradicts itself.' (Pei Songzhi's gloss.)

sentences.zh: 定軍潜行，卒出其南。

translations.literal: He steadied the army by secret march and suddenly emerged on their south.
translations.idiomatic: He slipped his column south and burst into their flank.

sentences.zh: 维乃缘山突至，泰與交戰，维退還。

translations.literal: Jiang Wei then came along the mountain in a sudden rush; Tai joined battle with him, and Jiang Wei withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wei clawed up the slope; Tai met him blade to blade and forced him back.

sentences.zh: 凉州軍從金城南至沃干阪。

translations.literal: The Liangzhou army marched from Jincheng south to the Wo'gan Slope.
translations.idiomatic: The Liangzhou corps marched south from Jincheng toward the Wo'gan Slope.

sentences.zh: 泰與经共密期，当共向其還路，维等聞之，遂遁，城中將士得出。

translations.literal: Tai and Jing secretly agreed to strike together at the enemy's line of retreat; when Jiang Wei and his men heard of it they fled, and the officers and men in the city were able to get out.
translations.idiomatic: Tai and Wang Jing coordinated a pincer on the retreat; Jiang Wei bolted at the news, and Didao's defenders poured free.

sentences.zh: 经叹曰：「粮不至旬，向不應机，舉城屠裂，覆喪一州矣。

translations.literal: Jing sighed, 'Our grain would not have lasted ten days; had you not seized the moment, the whole city would have been slaughtered and a whole province lost.'
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jing sighed, 'We had less than ten days' food; a moment's hesitation would have meant massacre and the loss of an entire province.'

sentences.zh: 」泰慰劳將士，前後遣還，更差軍守，并治城垒，還屯上邽。

translations.literal: Tai comforted the officers and men, sent them back in relays before and behind, reassigned troops to garrison the place, repaired walls and ramparts, and returned to camp at Shanggui.
translations.idiomatic: Tai rallied the troops, rotated them home in shifts, left fresh garrisons, rebuilt the walls, and withdrew to Shanggui.

sentences.zh: 初，泰聞经见圍，以州軍將士素皆一心，加得保城，非维所能卒倾。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Tai heard that Jing was besieged, because the provincial army had always been of one heart and moreover held a defensible city, he did not believe Jiang Wei could overturn it in a hurry.
translations.idiomatic: When Tai first learned of the siege, he trusted the Yongzhou troops' unity and the city's strength and doubted Jiang Wei could storm it overnight.

sentences.zh: 表上进軍晨夜速到還。

translations.literal: He memorialized for permission to advance, expecting to reach the field day and night.
translations.idiomatic: He asked leave to march, promising to arrive at forced marches.

sentences.zh: 众议以经奔北，城不足自固，维若断凉州之道，兼四郡民夷，据關、陇之险，敢能没经軍而屠陇右。

translations.literal: The assembly argued that Jing had been routed northward, the city could not hold itself, and if Jiang Wei cut the road to Liangzhou, combined the people and tribes of the four commanderies, and held the passes of Guan and Long, he could annihilate Jing's army and butcher all west of Long.
translations.idiomatic: Court opinion held that Wang Jing's defeat left Didao indefensible; if Jiang Wei severed the Liangzhou road, rallied the four commanderies of Han and tribesmen, and seized Tong Pass and Longxi, he might wipe out Wang Jing's force and scour the west.

sentences.zh: 宜须大兵四集，乃致攻討。

translations.literal: It was fitting to wait until great armies gathered on four sides before undertaking attack.
translations.idiomatic: They urged waiting until reinforcements converged from every quarter.

sentences.zh: 大將軍司马文王曰：「昔諸葛亮常有此志，卒亦不能。

translations.literal: The grand general Sima Zhao said, 'Long ago Zhuge Liang often cherished this ambition, yet in the end could not achieve it.
translations.idiomatic: Grand General Sima Zhao replied, 'Zhuge Liang nursed the same dream and never pulled it off.'

sentences.zh: 事大謀遠，非维所任也。

translations.literal: The affair is too great and the plan too distant—it lies beyond what Jiang Wei can shoulder.
translations.idiomatic: The scheme is too vast for Jiang Wei's shoulders.

sentences.zh: 且城非仓卒所拔，而粮少爲急，征西速救，得上策矣。
