translations.literal: Moreover a city cannot be stormed in haste, while grain shortage is the urgent matter; the western expedition's rapid rescue is the upper strategy.'
translations.idiomatic: Cities do not fall in a day, but hunger strikes at once—speed is the winning move.'

sentences.zh: 」泰每以一方有事，辄以虚声扰动天下，故希简白上事，驿書不过六百里。

translations.literal: Tai, whenever there was trouble in one region, was apt to raise empty alarms that disturbed the whole realm, and therefore he rarely reported matters in detail to the throne, keeping courier dispatches under six hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: Tai habitually muted his memorials so as not to panic the court—his express riders rarely exceeded six hundred li a day.

sentences.zh: 司马文王语荀顗曰：「玄伯沈勇能断，荷方伯之重，救將陷之城，而不求益兵，又希简上事，必能办贼故也。

translations.literal: Sima Zhao said to Xun Yi, 'Xuanbo is deep, brave, and decisive; bearing the weight of a regional command, he rescued a city on the verge of capture yet sought no extra troops and rarely troubled the capital with reports—surely because he knew he could finish the bandits himself.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Zhao told Xun Yi, 'Xuanbo combines grit and judgment; holding a border, he saved a doomed city without begging for reinforcements or flooding Luoyang with dispatches—he was certain he could handle Jiang Wei.'

sentences.zh: 都督大將，不当尔邪！」

translations.literal: Should a commander-in-chief not be thus!'
translations.idiomatic: That is how a supreme commander ought to behave!'

sentences.zh: 後徵泰爲尚書右仆射，典選舉，加侍中光禄大夫。

translations.literal: Later Tai was summoned as right vice-director of the Masters of Writing, placed in charge of appointments, and given additional rank as palace attendant and grand master for splendid happiness.
translations.idiomatic: Later the court recalled him as right vice-director of the Masters of Writing with charge of personnel, adding palace attendant and grand master for splendid happiness.

sentences.zh: 吴大將孫峻出淮、泗。

translations.literal: Wu grand general Sun Jun issued forth toward the Huai and Si rivers.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jun of Wu drove his host toward the Huai and Si.

sentences.zh: 以泰爲镇軍將軍，假节都督淮北諸軍事，诏徐州监軍已下受泰节度。

translations.literal: Tai was made general who guards the army, granted the staff of authority, and placed in overall command of all military affairs north of the Huai; an edict ordered the military overseer of Xu Province downward to accept Tai's orders.
translations.idiomatic: Tai was named general who guards the army, given the credential staff, and put in charge of all forces north of the Huai; edict made every overseer from Xu Province down answer to him.

sentences.zh: 峻退，軍還，转爲左仆射。

translations.literal: When Jun withdrew the army returned, and Tai was transferred to left vice-director.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jun retreated; Tai rotated home to left vice-director.

sentences.zh: 諸葛诞作乱寿春，司马文王率六軍軍丘头，泰总署行台。

translations.literal: Zhuge Dan rebelled at Shouchun; Sima Zhao led the six hosts to Qiuqiu, and Tai directed the mobile headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuge Dan rose at Shouchun, Sima Zhao marched the six armies to Qiuqiu while Tai ran the forward command post.

sentences.zh: 司马景王、文王皆與泰亲友，及沛國武陔亦與泰善。

translations.literal: Sima Shi, Sima Zhao, and Tai were all intimate friends, and Wu Zhi of Pei was also close to Tai.
translations.idiomatic: Both Sima brothers counted Tai among their confidants, as did Wu Zhi of Pei.

sentences.zh: 文王问陔曰：「玄伯何如其父司空也？

translations.literal: Zhao asked Zhi, 'How does Xuanbo compare with his father the minister of works?'
translations.idiomatic: Sima Zhao asked Wu Zhi, 'How does Xuanbo measure against his father the minister of works?'

sentences.zh: 」陔曰：「通雅博暢，能以天下声教爲己任者，不如也；

translations.literal: Zhi replied, 'In comprehensive elegance and making the empire's moral instruction one's own burden, he does not match;
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zhi answered, 'In breadth of culture and shouldering the empire's moral teaching, he falls short;'

sentences.zh: 明统简至，立功立事，过之。

translations.literal: in clarifying systems, cutting to essentials, establishing merit, and accomplishing deeds, he surpasses him.'
translations.idiomatic: in sorting institutions, grasping essentials, winning battles, and finishing tasks, he surpasses him.'

sentences.zh: 」泰前後以功增邑二千六百户，赐子弟一人亭侯，二人關内侯。

translations.literal: Tai was enfeoffed with an additional two thousand six hundred households for successive merits, and one son was given village marquis while two received secondary marquis within the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Merit raised his fief by 2,600 households; one son took a village marquisate and two became secondary marquises within the passes.

sentences.zh: 景元元年薨，追赠司空。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingyuan he died and was posthumously honored as minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Jingyuan 1 and was posthumously named minister of works.

sentences.zh: 谥曰穆侯。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Marquis Mu.
translations.idiomatic: He received the posthumous title Marquis Mu.

sentences.zh: 〈干宝《晋纪》曰：高贵乡公之杀，司马文王会朝臣谋其故。

translations.literal: Gan Bao's Jin Annals states: After the murder of the duke of Gaoxiang, Sima Zhao assembled the court to debate the cause.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Bao's Jin Annals records that after the killing of the duke of Gaoxiang, Sima Zhao convened the ministers to assign blame.

sentences.zh: 太常陈泰不至，使其舅荀顗召之。

translations.literal: Grand master of ceremonies Chen Tai did not appear, so Zhao had his uncle Xun Yi summon him.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Master of Ceremonies Chen Tai stayed away until Sima Zhao sent his uncle Xun Yi to fetch him.

sentences.zh: 顗至，告以可否。

translations.literal: When Yi arrived he explained whether Tai should go or not.
translations.idiomatic: Yi explained what was at stake.

sentences.zh: 泰曰：“世之论者，以泰方於舅，今舅不如泰也。

translations.literal: Tai said, 'Those who discuss the age compare me with my uncle; today my uncle does not match me.'
translations.idiomatic: Tai said, 'Gossip pairs me with my uncle; today the uncle cuts the poorer figure.'

sentences.zh: ”子弟内外咸共逼之，垂涕而入。

translations.literal: Sons, nephews, inside and outside, all together pressed him; weeping, he entered.
translations.idiomatic: Kin inside and outside pressed him until, in tears, he went in.

sentences.zh: 王待之曲室，谓曰：“玄伯，卿何以处我？

translations.literal: The king received him in a side chamber and said, 'Xuanbo, how will you deal with me?'
translations.idiomatic: The regent met him in a private room: 'Xuanbo, what do you intend for me?'

sentences.zh: ”对曰：“诛贾充以谢天下。

translations.literal: He answered, 'Execute Jia Chong to apologize to the realm.'
translations.idiomatic: Tai answered, 'Execute Jia Chong and apologize to the empire.'

sentences.zh: ”文王曰：“为我更思其次。

translations.literal: Zhao said, 'Think again of something next below that.'
translations.idiomatic: Zhao said, 'Give me a lesser remedy.'

sentences.zh: ”泰曰：“泰言惟有进於此，不知其次。

translations.literal: Tai said, 'My words can only go higher than this; I know no second step.'
translations.idiomatic: Tai replied, 'I have nothing milder to offer—only sterner.'

sentences.zh: ”文王乃不更言。

translations.literal: Zhao then spoke no further.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao fell silent.

sentences.zh: 魏氏春秋曰：帝之崩也，太傅司马孚、尚书右仆射陈泰枕帝尸於股，号哭尽哀。

translations.literal: The Spring and Autumn of Wei states: When the emperor collapsed, grand tutor Sima Fu and right vice-director of the Masters of Writing Chen Tai pillowed the imperial corpse on their thighs and wailed their grief to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Spring and Autumn adds that at the emperor's death Sima Fu and Chen Tai cradled the body on their laps and keened without restraint.

sentences.zh: 时大将军入于禁中，泰见之悲恸，大将军亦对之泣，谓曰：“玄伯，其如我何？

translations.literal: At that time the grand general entered the forbidden palace; Tai, seeing him, was overcome with grief, and the grand general wept in turn, saying to him, 'Xuanbo, what am I to do?'
translations.idiomatic: When the grand general entered the inner palace, Tai confronted him in anguish; the general wept as well, asking, 'Xuanbo, what becomes of us?'

sentences.zh: ”泰曰：“独有斩贾充，少可以谢天下耳。

translations.literal: Tai said, 'Only by beheading Jia Chong could one slightly apologize to the realm.'
translations.idiomatic: Tai said, 'Only Jia Chong's head would begin to appease the world.'

sentences.zh: ”大将军久之曰：“卿更思其他。

translations.literal: After a long while the grand general said, 'Think of something else.'
translations.idiomatic: After a long pause the general said, 'Think of another way.'

sentences.zh: ”泰曰：“岂可使泰复发后言。

translations.literal: Tai said, 'How could you make me speak a second time?'
translations.idiomatic: Tai answered, 'You cannot make me repeat myself.'

sentences.zh: ”遂呕血薨。

translations.literal: Thereupon he vomited blood and died.
translations.idiomatic: He spat blood and died.

sentences.zh: 臣松之案本传，泰不为太常，未详干宝所由知之。

translations.literal: Your subject Songzhi notes that according to this biography Tai was not grand master of ceremonies; it is unclear how Gan Bao knew this.
translations.idiomatic: Songzhi remarks: the main text never makes Tai grand master of ceremonies—Gan Bao's source is obscure.

sentences.zh: 孙盛改易泰言，虽为小胜。

translations.literal: Sun Sheng's alterations to Tai's words, though a small improvement.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng's rewrite of Tai's words is a slight polish,

sentences.zh: 然检盛言诸所改易，皆非别有异闻，率更自以意制，多不如旧。

translations.literal: yet examining Sheng's changes, none rest on a different tradition; for the most part he invented out of his own opinion, and most do not match the old text.
translations.idiomatic: yet none of his variants rest on new evidence—mostly private invention—and usually fall short of the original.

sentences.zh: 凡记言之体，当使若出其口。

translations.literal: As a rule the form for recording speech ought to make it seem as if it issued from the speaker's mouth.
translations.idiomatic: Recorded speech should read as if spoken aloud.

sentences.zh: 辞胜而违实，固君子所不取，况复不胜而徒长虚妄哉？

translations.literal: When phrasing triumphs but violates fact, that is something a gentleman does not take; how much more when it does not triumph but only lengthens falsehood?'
translations.idiomatic: Elegant words that twist truth are bad enough; worse are clumsy inventions that only multiply lies.'

sentences.zh: 案博物记曰：太丘长陈寔、寔子鸿胪纪、纪子司空群、群子泰四世，於汉、魏二朝并有重名，而其德渐渐小减。

translations.literal: The Bowu ji states: Magistrate of Taiqiu Chen Shi, his son grand herald Ji, Ji's son minister of works Qun, and Qun's son Tai—four generations in succession had great fame in Han and Wei, yet their virtue gradually diminished.
translations.idiomatic: The Bowu ji notes four generations—Shi, Ji, Qun, Tai—celebrated in both dynasties, with virtue thinning each step down.

sentences.zh: 时人为其语曰：“公惭卿，卿惭长。

translations.literal: Men of the time made a rhyme of it: 'The duke is ashamed before the minister; the minister is ashamed before the elder.'
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries sang, 'The lord blushes before the minister; the minister before the elder.'
'. (End of Pei Songzhi's note.)

sentences.zh: 子恂嗣。

translations.literal: His son Xun succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xun inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 恂薨，无嗣。

translations.literal: When Xun died there was no heir.
translations.idiomatic: Xun died without issue.

sentences.zh: 弟温紹封。

translations.literal: His younger brother Wen succeeded to the fief.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Chen Wen inherited the enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 咸熙中开建五等，以泰著勋前朝，改封温爲慎子。

translations.literal: In the Xianxi era, when the five grades of nobility were instituted, because Tai had earned merit under the previous reign, Wen was reassigned the fief and enfeoffed as zi-ranked noble of Shen.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei established its five-tier peerage in Xianxi, the court re-enfeoffed Chen Wen as baron (zi) of Shen in honor of Chen Tai's service to the fallen dynasty.

sentences.zh: 〈案陈氏谱：群之后，名位遂微。

translations.literal: According to the Chen lineage register, after Qun the family's names and offices gradually declined.
translations.idiomatic: The Chen genealogy notes that after Chen Qun's generation rank and visibility slowly thinned.

sentences.zh: 谌孙佐，官至青州刺史。

translations.literal: Chen's grandson Zuo rose to the post of inspector of Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zuo, a grandson of the line, became inspector of Qing Province.

sentences.zh: 佐弟坦，廷尉。

translations.literal: Zuo's younger brother Tan became minister of justice.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Chen Tan served as minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 佐子准，太尉，封广陵郡公。

translations.literal: Zuo's son Zhun became grand commandant and was enfeoffed duke of Guangling commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zhun, Zuo's son, reached grand commandant and received the ducal patent for Guangling commandery.

sentences.zh: 准弟戴、徵及从弟堪，并至大位。

translations.literal: Zhun's younger brothers Dai and Zheng, together with his cousin Kan, all rose to high office.
translations.idiomatic: Zhun's brothers Dai and Zheng and his cousin Kan each climbed to exalted posts.

sentences.zh: 准孙逵，字林道，有誉江左，为西中郎将，追赠卫将军。〉

translations.literal: Zhun's grandson Kui, courtesy name Lindao, enjoyed reputation in the lands east of the Yangzi; he served as general of the central west and was posthumously honored as guards general.
translations.idiomatic: Zhun's grandson Kui, style Lindao, was celebrated in Jiangnan, commanded the central-western host, and was canonized posthumously as guards general.

sentences.zh: 陳矫字季弼，广陵东阳人也。

translations.literal: Chen Jiao, courtesy name Jibi, was a native of Dongyang in Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jiao, whose courtesy name was Jibi, came from Dongyang in Guangling commandery.

sentences.zh: 避乱江东及东城，辭孫策、袁术之命，還本郡。

translations.literal: To flee disorder he went to the lands east of the Yangzi and to Dongcheng, declined summons from Sun Ce and Yuan Shu, and returned to his home commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He fled the wars to Jiangdong and Dongcheng, refused appointments from Sun Ce and Yuan Shu, and went home.

sentences.zh: 太守陳登请爲功曹，使矫詣许，謂曰：「许下论议，待吾不足；

translations.literal: Grand Warden Chen Deng requested him as merit clerk and sent Jiao to Xu, saying, 'The talk at the capital thinks they do not treat me generously enough;
translations.idiomatic: Chen Deng made him merit clerk and dispatched him to the capital with this charge: 'Rumor in Xu says the court undervalues me—

sentences.zh: 足下相爲观察，還以见诲。

translations.literal: you observe on my behalf and return to instruct me.'
translations.idiomatic: go see for yourself and report back what I should learn.'

sentences.zh: 」矫還曰：「聞遠近之论，颇謂明府骄而自矜。

translations.literal: Jiao returned and said, 'I hear men far and near say that you, sir, are arrogant and full of self-regard.'
translations.idiomatic: Jiao came back and said, 'From every quarter I hear that you, my lord, are proud and self-satisfied.'

sentences.zh: 」登曰：「夫闺门雍穆，有德有行，吾敬陳元方兄弟；

translations.literal: Deng said, 'As for harmony within the women's quarters, possessing virtue and conduct—I respect the brothers Chen Yuanfang;
translations.idiomatic: Deng answered, 'In the grace of a well-ordered household, in moral weight—I honor Chen Ji and his brothers;

sentences.zh: 渊清玉絜，有礼有法，吾敬华子鱼；

translations.literal: deep as an abyss, pure as jade, possessing ritual and law—I respect Hua Ziyu;
translations.idiomatic: in clarity of principle and ritual discipline—I honor Hua Xin;

sentences.zh: 清脩疾恶，有识有義，吾敬趙元达；

translations.literal: pure in cultivation and hating evil, possessing insight and righteousness—I respect Zhao Yuanda;
translations.idiomatic: in stern integrity and hatred of vice—I honor Zhao Yuanda;

sentences.zh: 博聞强记，奇逸卓荦，吾敬孔文舉；

translations.literal: broad of learning and strong of memory, strange and outstanding—I respect Kong Wenju;
translations.idiomatic: in encyclopedic memory and soaring talent—I honor Kong Rong;

sentences.zh: 雄姿杰出，有王霸之略，吾敬劉玄德：所敬如此，何骄之有！

translations.literal: heroic in bearing and preeminent, possessing the strategy of a king or hegemon—I respect Liu Xuande: such are those I respect—what arrogance is there!
translations.idiomatic: in heroic stature and the vision of a founder—I honor Liu Bei. These are the men I revere—where is the arrogance?'

sentences.zh: 餘子琐琐，亦焉足录哉？

translations.literal: The rest are petty and trifling—are they worth recording?'
translations.idiomatic: As for lesser men, they are too small to mention.'

sentences.zh: 」登雅意如此，而深敬友矫。

translations.literal: Deng's lofty intent was thus, yet he deeply respected and befriended Jiao.
translations.idiomatic: Such was Deng's self-image, yet he esteemed Jiao as a close friend.

sentences.zh: 郡爲孫权所圍於匡奇，登令矫求救於太祖。

translations.literal: The commandery was besieged by Sun Quan at Kuangqi; Deng ordered Jiao to beg rescue from the Grand Progenitor.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Quan penned the commandery at Kuangqi, Deng sent Jiao through the lines to plead for aid from Cao Cao.

sentences.zh: 矫說太祖曰：「鄙郡雖小，形便之國也，若蒙救援，使爲外籓，則吴人剉謀，徐方永安，武声遠震，仁爱滂流，未從之國，望风景附，崇德养威，此王业也。

translations.literal: Jiao urged the Grand Progenitor, saying, 'Though my humble commandery is small, it is a country of favorable terrain; if it receives your rescue and is made an outer screen, then Wu's designs will be blunted, the Xu region will be forever secure, martial renown will shake the distance, benevolent love will pour abroad, and states not yet following will look to the wind and attach themselves—honoring virtue and nurturing awe: this is the work of a royal enterprise.'
translations.idiomatic: Jiao told Cao Cao, 'Our small district sits on strategic ground; rescue us and make us your outer shield, and you blunt Wu's ambitions, secure the Huai basin, spread your fame, and draw wavering lords to your banner—that is how true kingship is built.'

sentences.zh: 」太祖奇矫，欲留之。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor marveled at Jiao and wished to retain him.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao was impressed and wanted to keep him at headquarters.

sentences.zh: 矫辭曰：「本國倒县，本奔走告急，纵无申胥之效，敢忘弘演之義乎？」

translations.literal: Jiao declined, saying, 'My state hangs upside down; I came running to report emergency; even if I lack Shen Baoxu's effect, how dare I forget the righteousness of Hong Yan?'
translations.idiomatic: Jiao refused: 'My home hangs by a thread; I came as a messenger of distress. I am no Shen Baoxu, yet I cannot betray the loyalty of Hong Yan.'

sentences.zh: 〈刘向《新序》曰：齐桓公求婚於卫，卫不与，而嫁於许。

translations.literal: Liu Xiang's Xin Xu states: Duke Huan of Qi sought a marriage alliance with Wei; Wei refused and gave the bride to Xu instead.
translations.idiomatic: The Xin Xu records that Duke Huan of Qi asked Wei for a bride; Wei refused and married her to the lord of Xu.

sentences.zh: 卫为狄所伐，桓公不救，至於国灭君死。

translations.literal: When Wei was attacked by the Di, Huan did not rescue them, until the state perished and the ruler died.
translations.idiomatic: When the Di overran Wei, Huan held back until the state fell and its lord perished.

sentences.zh: 懿公尸为狄人所食，惟有肝在。

translations.literal: Lord Yi's corpse was eaten by the Di; only the liver remained.
translations.idiomatic: The Di devoured Duke Yi's body until only his liver was left.

sentences.zh: 懿公有臣曰弘演，適使反，致命於肝曰：“君为其内，臣为其外。

translations.literal: Lord Yi had a minister named Hong Yan, who was returning from a mission, laid the mandate on the liver, and said, 'Let the lord be within and the minister without.'
translations.idiomatic: Minister Hong Yan, returning from embassy, placed the charge upon the liver, declaring, 'The ruler dwells within; the servant guards the outer world.'

sentences.zh: ”乃刳腹内肝而死。

translations.literal: Thereupon he cut open his belly, placed the liver inside, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He ripped open his own belly, inserted the liver, and died.

sentences.zh: 齐桓公曰：“卫有臣若此而尚灭，寡人无有，亡无日矣！

translations.literal: Duke Huan of Qi said, 'If Wei had ministers like this and still perished, I have none—my doom cannot be far!'
translations.idiomatic: Huan of Qi cried, 'Wei fell though it had such servants; I have none—my end is near!'

sentences.zh: ”乃救卫，定其君。〉

translations.literal: Thereupon he rescued Wei and established its ruler.'〉
translations.idiomatic: He then marched to restore Wei and set its lord back on the throne.' (End of Xin Xu quotation.)

sentences.zh: 太祖乃遣赴救。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor thereupon sent him to hurry the relief.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao sent Jiao back to speed the rescue.

sentences.zh: 吴軍既退，登多设间伏，勒兵追奔，大破之。

translations.literal: After Wu's army withdrew, Deng laid many ambushes, led troops in pursuit of the fleeing foe, and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu lifted the siege, Deng planted ambushes, chased the retreating host, and shattered it.

sentences.zh: 子本嗣，历位郡守、九卿。

translations.literal: His son Ben succeeded, successively holding the posts of grand warden and one of the nine ministers.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chen Ben inherited the title and rose through grand wardencies to the nine high ministers.

sentences.zh: 所在操纲领，舉大体，能使羣下自尽。

translations.literal: Wherever he served he grasped the guiding principles and attended to the great pattern, enabling those below him to exhaust their abilities.
translations.idiomatic: In every office he set policy and left detail to subordinates, who then gave their best.

sentences.zh: 有统御之才，不亲小事，不读法律而得廷尉之称，優於司马岐等，精练文理。

translations.literal: He had talent for command and control, did not personally attend to petty affairs, did not study the statutes yet won the reputation of minister of justice—superior to Sima Qi and the like—in mastery of legal reasoning.
translations.idiomatic: He commanded men without micromanaging, never cracked a law code yet was hailed as a natural minister of justice, outshining Sima Qi in juridical clarity.

sentences.zh: 遷镇北將軍，假节都督河北諸軍事。

translations.literal: He was promoted to general who guards the north, granted the staff of authority, and placed in overall command of all military affairs north of the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: He became general who guards the north with the credential staff and supreme command north of the river.

sentences.zh: 薨，子粲嗣。

translations.literal: When he died his son Can succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: At his death his son Chen Can inherited the line.

sentences.zh: 本弟骞，咸熙中爲车骑將軍。

translations.literal: Ben's younger brother Qian became general of chariots and cavalry in the Xianxi era.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Ben's brother Qian rose to general of chariots and cavalry under Xianxi.

sentences.zh: 〈案晋书曰：骞字休渊，为晋佐命功臣，至太傅，封高平郡公。〉

translations.literal: According to the Jin History, Qian, courtesy name Xiuyuan, was a founding merit minister of Jin, rose to grand tutor, and was enfeoffed duke of Gaoping commandery.'〉
translations.idiomatic: The Jinshu adds that Qian, style Xiuyuan, helped found the Jin dynasty, became grand tutor, and was made duke of Gaoping.'

sentences.zh: 初，矫爲郡功曹，使过泰山。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Jiao was merit clerk of the commandery, he passed through Taishan.
translations.idiomatic: Long before, as commandery merit clerk, Jiao traveled through Taishan.

sentences.zh: 泰山太守东郡薛悌異之，結爲亲友。

translations.literal: Grand Warden of Taishan Xue Ti of Dongjun marveled at him and formed a bond of close friendship.
translations.idiomatic: Taishan Grand Warden Xue Ti of Dongjun was struck with admiration and befriended him.

sentences.zh: 戏謂矫曰：「以郡吏而交二千石，邻國君屈從陪臣游，不亦可乎！

translations.literal: Ti joked to Jiao, 'For a commandery clerk to befriend a two-thousand-dan official—may a neighboring state's lord condescend to roam with a petty minister—is that not fitting!'
translations.idiomatic: Ti teased him: 'A petty clerk befriending a two-thousand-dan grand warden—like a prince strolling with a vassal—is that not a fine joke?'

sentences.zh: 」悌後爲魏郡及尚書令，皆承代矫云。

translations.literal: Later Ti became grand warden of Wei commandery and director of the Masters of Writing, and in both cases succeeded Jiao in office, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Later Xue Ti served as grand warden of Wei and director of the Masters of Writing—each time, tradition says, stepping into Jiao's shoes.

sentences.zh: 〈《世语》曰：悌字孝威。

translations.literal: The Shiyu states: Ti, courtesy name Xiaowei.
translations.idiomatic: The Shiyu gives Ti's style as Xiaowei.

sentences.zh: 年二十二，以兗州从事为泰山太守。

translations.literal: At age twenty-two he became grand warden of Taishan from clerk of Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty-two he leapt from Yan Province clerk to grand warden of Taishan.

sentences.zh: 初，太祖定冀州，以悌及东平王国为左右长史，后至中领军，并悉忠贞练事，为世吏表。〉

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Grand Progenitor pacified Ji Province, he appointed Ti and Wang Guo of Dongping as left and right senior clerks; later they reached central commandant of the army, both utterly loyal and practiced in affairs, models for clerks of the age.'〉
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao took Ji Province he named Ti and Wang Guo of Dongping his left and right senior clerks; both rose to central commandant, loyal and efficient exemplars for every clerk.'

sentences.zh: 徐宣字宝堅，广陵海西人也。

translations.literal: Xu Xuan, courtesy name Baojian, was a native of Haixi in Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Xuan, style Baojian, hailed from Haixi in Guangling.

sentences.zh: 避乱江东，又辭孫策之命，還本郡。

translations.literal: He fled disorder to the east of the Yangzi and again declined Sun Ce's summons, returning to his home commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Like Jiao he fled to Jiangdong, refused Sun Ce's call, and went home.

sentences.zh: 與陳矫并爲纲纪，二人齊名而私好不协，然俱见器於太守陳登，與登并心於太祖。

translations.literal: Together with Chen Jiao he served as chief clerk; the two were equal in fame though privately they did not get along, yet both were esteemed by Grand Warden Chen Deng, and together with Deng they gave their hearts to the Grand Progenitor.
translations.idiomatic: He and Chen Jiao shared the chief clerk's burden—rivals in reputation if not in friendship—yet Deng valued both, and each pledged himself to Cao Cao.

sentences.zh: 海西、淮浦二县民作乱，都尉卫弥、令梁习夜奔宣家，密送免之。

translations.literal: The people of Haixi and Huaipu commanderies rose in revolt; commandant Wei Mi and magistrate Liang Xi fled by night to Xuan's house, who secretly saw them off to safety.
translations.idiomatic: When Haixi and Huaipu rose, Commandant Wei Mi and Magistrate Liang Xi slipped to Xuan's door; he smuggled them to safety.

sentences.zh: 太祖遣督軍扈质來討贼，以兵少不进。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor sent army overseer Hu Zhi to punish the bandits, but with few troops he did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao sent overseer Hu Zhi to crush the rebels, but Zhi stalled for lack of numbers.

sentences.zh: 宣潜见责之，示以形勢，质乃进破贼。

translations.literal: Xuan secretly visited and rebuked him, showed him the strategic situation, and Zhi then advanced and broke the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan cornered Zhi, laid out the map of force, and Zhi marched and routed the rebels.

sentences.zh: 太祖辟爲司空掾属，除东缗、发干令，遷齊郡太守，入爲门下督，從到寿春。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor summoned him as subordinate to the minister of works, appointed him magistrate of Dongmin and Fagan, promoted him to grand warden of Qi commandery, brought him in as gatehouse commander, and followed him to Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao took him on as ministerial clerk, named him magistrate of Dongmin and Fagan, raised him to grand warden of Qi, then brought him to court as gatehouse commander for the Shouchun campaign.

sentences.zh: 會马超作乱，大軍西征，太祖见官属曰：「今当遠征，而此方未定，以爲後忧，宜得清公大德以镇统之。

translations.literal: It happened that Ma Chao rebelled and the great army marched west; the Grand Progenitor told his officials, 'We are about to campaign far while this region is still unsettled—I fear it as a trouble in the rear; we need a pure, fair man of great virtue to hold and command it.'
translations.idiomatic: When Ma Chao rose and the host marched west, Cao Cao told his staff, 'I leave with the west still unquiet; I need a man of spotless honor to hold this ground.'

sentences.zh: 」乃以宣爲左护軍，留统諸軍。

translations.literal: Thereupon he appointed Xuan as left protector of the army and left him to command all troops.
translations.idiomatic: He named Xuan left protector of the army and left him in charge of the rear echelon.

sentences.zh: 還，爲丞相东曹掾，出爲魏郡太守。

translations.literal: On return he became senior clerk to the eastern bureau of the chancellor, then went out as grand warden of Wei commandery.
translations.idiomatic: After the western campaign he became eastern-bureau senior clerk under the chancellor, then grand warden of Wei.

sentences.zh: 太祖崩洛阳，羣臣入殿中发哀。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor died at Luoyang the ministers entered the hall to voice their grief.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao died at Luoyang the courtiers entered the palace to mourn.

sentences.zh: 或言可易諸城守，用谯、沛人。

translations.literal: Some said the garrisons of the various cities could be replaced with men from Qiao and Pei.
translations.idiomatic: Some proposed replacing every city garrison with troops from Qiao and Pei.

sentences.zh: 宣厉声曰：「今者遠近一统，人怀效节，何必谯、沛，而沮宿卫者心。

translations.literal: Xuan spoke sternly, 'Now near and far are unified and every man cherishes the wish to repay obligation—why must it be Qiao and Pei, and so dishearten the long-serving guards?'
translations.idiomatic: Xuan thundered back, 'The realm is one; every soldier burns to serve—why insult the old guard by swapping in only men from Qiao and Pei?'

sentences.zh: 」文帝聞曰：「所謂社稷之臣也。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen heard it he said, 'This is what is called a minister of the altars of soil and grain.'
translations.idiomatic: Wendi heard the story and said, 'There speaks a true pillar of state.'

sentences.zh: 」帝既践阼，爲御史中丞，赐爵關内侯，徙城门校尉，旬月遷司隶校尉，转散骑常侍。

translations.literal: After the emperor ascended the throne Xuan became palace aide to the censor-in-chief, was granted secondary marquis within the passes, was transferred to colonel of the city gates, within ten days was promoted to metropolitan commandant, then rotated to standing attendant-in-ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Once Wendi took the throne Xuan became palace aide to the censor-in-chief, won secondary marquis within the passes, jumped to colonel of the gates within a month, then metropolitan commandant, then standing attendant.

sentences.zh: 從至广陵，六軍乘舟，风浪暴起，帝船回倒，宣病在後，陵波而前，羣寮莫先至者。

translations.literal: He followed the emperor to Guangling; the six armies boarded boats, wind and waves suddenly rose, the emperor's ship spun and capsized, while Xuan, ill in the rear ships, breasted the waves and went forward—none of the assembly reached him first.
translations.idiomatic: On the Guangling tour the imperial flotilla met a squall; the dragon boat spun while Xuan, sick in the rear squadron, pulled ahead of every courtier through the surf.

sentences.zh: 帝壮之，遷尚書。

translations.literal: The emperor admired him and promoted him to the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his courage and moved him into the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 明帝即位，封津阳亭侯，邑二百户。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming took the throne he was enfeoffed as village marquis of Jinyang with two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Mingdi enfeoffed him village marquis of Jinyang at two hundred households.

sentences.zh: 中领軍桓范荐宣曰：

translations.literal: Central commandant Huan Fan recommended Xuan, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Huan Fan, central commandant, memorialized on Xuan's behalf:

sentences.zh: 臣闻帝王用人，度世授才，争夺之时，以策略为先，分定之后，以忠义为首。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that emperors employ men by sizing the age and assigning talent: in times of struggle strategy comes first; after division is fixed loyalty comes first.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that wise kings match talent to the times—in war, stratagem; in peace, steadfast loyalty.

sentences.zh: 故晋文行舅犯之计而赏雍季之言，

translations.literal: Therefore Duke Wen of Jin acted on Jiu Fan's plan yet rewarded Yong Ji's words.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Duke Wen of Jin followed Jiu Fan's ruse yet ranked Yong Ji's honest counsel higher in the reward rolls.

sentences.zh: 〈《吕氏春秋》曰：昔晋文公将与楚人战於城濮，召咎犯而问曰：“楚众我寡，奈何而可？

translations.literal: The Lüshi Chunqiu states: Long ago Duke Wen of Jin was about to fight Chu at Chengpu; he summoned Jiu Fan and asked, 'Chu's host is many and ours few—how may we prevail?'
translations.idiomatic: The Lüshi Chunqiu tells how Duke Wen of Jin, facing Chu at Chengpu, asked Jiu Fan, 'They outnumber us—what now?'

sentences.zh: ”咎犯对曰：“臣闻繁礼之君，不足於文，繁战之君，不足於诈，君亦诈之而已。

translations.literal: Jiu Fan answered, 'Your subject has heard that a lord fond of elaborate ritual is short on culture, and a lord fond of many battles is short on craft—my lord need only answer craft with craft.'
translations.idiomatic: Jiu Fan answered, 'A ruler who loves pageantry lacks true refinement; a warrior who loves battle lacks true guile—meet guile with guile.'

sentences.zh: ”文公以咎犯言告雍季，雍季曰：“竭泽而渔，岂不得鱼，而明年无鱼。

translations.literal: Duke Wen reported Jiu Fan's words to Yong Ji, and Yong Ji said, 'To drain a marsh to fish may catch fish today, but next year there will be no fish.
translations.idiomatic: Wen repeated this to Yong Ji, who said, 'Drain the pond and you eat today but starve tomorrow.'

sentences.zh: 焚薮而田，岂不得兽，而明年无兽。

translations.literal: To burn the scrub and hunt may catch beasts today, but next year there will be no beasts.
translations.idiomatic: Burn the coverts and you bag game now but leave none for later.'

sentences.zh: 诈伪之道，虽今偷可，后将无复，非长术也。

translations.literal: The way of deceit, though it may steal a gain today, will not be repeatable later—it is no long-term method.'
translations.idiomatic: Trickery buys a moment; it cannot be a lasting policy.'

sentences.zh: ”文公用咎犯之言，而败楚人於城濮。

translations.literal: Duke Wen used Jiu Fan's words and defeated the men of Chu at Chengpu.
translations.idiomatic: Wen followed Jiu Fan and shattered Chu at Chengpu.'

sentences.zh: 反而为赏，雍季在上。

translations.literal: When he turned to grant rewards Yong Ji stood highest.
translations.idiomatic: When it came time for rewards Yong Ji stood first in line.'

sentences.zh: 左右谏曰：“城濮之功，咎犯之谋也。

translations.literal: Those at his side remonstrated, 'The merit at Chengpu was Jiu Fan's stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: Courtiers protested, 'Chengpu was Jiu Fan's victory.'

sentences.zh: 君用其言而后其身，或者不可乎！

translations.literal: You used his words yet place him behind—perhaps that cannot be right!'
translations.idiomatic: You took his counsel yet rank him last—how can that be just?'

sentences.zh: ”文公曰：“雍季之言，百代之利也；

translations.literal: Duke Wen said, 'Yong Ji's words are a benefit for a hundred generations;
translations.idiomatic: Wen answered, 'Yong Ji speaks for ages to come;

sentences.zh: 咎犯之言，一时之务也。

translations.literal: Jiu Fan's words are the business of a single moment.
translations.idiomatic: Jiu Fan speaks only for the crisis at hand.'

sentences.zh: 焉有以一时之务，先百代之砾乎？

translations.literal: How could there be putting the business of a single moment before the profit of a hundred generations?'
translations.idiomatic: How could I rank a day's tactic above a century's good?'
'. (End of Lüshi Chunqiu quotation.)

sentences.zh: 高祖用陈平之智而讬后於周勃也。

translations.literal: Gaozu used Chen Ping's cleverness yet entrusted the aftermath to Zhou Bo.
translations.idiomatic: Han Gaozu relied on Chen Ping's wit but left the aftermath to Zhou Bo's steadfast arm.

sentences.zh: 窃见尚书徐宣，体忠厚之行，秉直亮之性；

translations.literal: Your subject has observed Master of Writing Xu Xuan: his person embodies the conduct of loyalty and generosity and the nature of straightness and clarity.
translations.idiomatic: I see Director Xu Xuan: loyal, generous, blunt, and bright.

sentences.zh: 清雅特立，不拘世俗；

translations.literal: Pure and elegant, standing alone, he is not bound by vulgar convention.
translations.idiomatic: Refined and aloof, he scorns fashion.

sentences.zh: 确然难动，有社稷之节；

translations.literal: Firm and immovable, he possesses the integrity of the altars of soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: Rock-steady, he has the fiber of a pillar of state.

sentences.zh: 历位州郡，所在称职。

translations.literal: In successive posts in provinces and commanderies he was competent wherever he served.
translations.idiomatic: In province after province he proved equal to every charge.

sentences.zh: 今仆射缺，宣行掌后事；

translations.literal: Now the vice-directorship is vacant; Xuan is fit to take charge of the rear ministries.
translations.idiomatic: The vice-director's chair is empty; Xuan should fill it.

sentences.zh: 腹心任重，莫宜宣者。

translations.literal: For a weighty post at the ruler's heart and belly none matches Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: For a trust this heavy no man suits better.

sentences.zh: 帝遂以宣爲左仆射，後加侍中灌禄大夫。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon appointed Xuan as left vice-director and later added palace attendant and grand master for splendid happiness.
translations.idiomatic: Mingdi named him left vice-director, then added palace attendant and grand master for splendid happiness.

sentences.zh: 车驾幸许昌，总统留事。

translations.literal: When the imperial train visited Xuchang he presided over all affairs left behind.
translations.idiomatic: During the emperor's stay at Xuchang he ran the capital in absentia.

sentences.zh: 帝還，主者奏呈文書。

translations.literal: When the emperor returned the responsible officials presented memorials and documents.
translations.idiomatic: On the emperor's return the clerks piled memorials on his desk.

sentences.zh: 诏曰：「吾省與仆射禾異？

translations.literal: An edict said, 'What difference is there between my review and the vice director's?' (text: 禾 for 何).
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, 'How does my own review differ from the vice director's?'

sentences.zh: 」竟不视。

translations.literal: In the end he did not look at them.
translations.idiomatic: Mingdi never opened the files.

sentences.zh: 尚方令坐猥见考竟，宣上疏陳威刑大过，又諫作宫殿穷尽民力，帝皆手诏嘉納。

translations.literal: The director of the imperial workshops was impeached for a petty offense and tortured to death; Xuan submitted a memorial declaring that awesome punishments had gone too far, and again remonstrated against building palaces that exhausted the people's strength; the emperor personally wrote edicts praising and accepting all.
translations.idiomatic: When a palace artisan was flogged to death on a trifle, Xuan protested cruel justice and wasteful palace works; Mingdi answered each memorial with his own brush in praise.

sentences.zh: 宣曰：「七十有县车之礼，今已六十八，可以去矣。

translations.literal: Xuan said, 'At seventy there is the rite of hanging up the carriage; I am already sixty-eight—I may retire.'
translations.idiomatic: Xuan said, 'The rites let a man retire his carriage at seventy; I am sixty-eight and ready to step down.'

sentences.zh: 」乃固辭疾逊位，帝终不许。

translations.literal: Thereupon he firmly pleaded illness to yield his post, but the emperor in the end did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed a resignation on grounds of age; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 青龙四年薨，遺令布衣疏巾，敛以時服。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Qinglong he died, leaving instructions for plain cloth and a loose headcloth and burial in timely garments only.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Qinglong 4, ordering a plain hemp shroud and timely dress only for the coffin.

sentences.zh: 诏曰：「宣体履至实，直内方外，历在三朝，公亮正色，有讬孤寄命之节，可謂柱石臣也。

translations.literal: An edict said, 'Xuan's conduct pursued utmost sincerity; he was straight within and square without; through three reigns he was fair and bright in public mien, possessing the integrity of one who receives the orphan and entrusts his mandate—he may be called a pillar and cornerstone minister.
translations.idiomatic: The court eulogized him as blunt within, square without, loyal through three reigns, fit to receive a regency—the very model of a pillar minister.

sentences.zh: 常欲倚以台辅，未及登之，惜乎大命不永！

translations.literal: I always wished to lean on him as a terrace minister, yet had not yet elevated him—alas, great fate was not long!'
translations.idiomatic: I meant to raise him to chancellor but heaven cut him short.'

sentences.zh: 其追赠车骑將軍，葬如公礼。

translations.literal: Let him be posthumously honored as general of chariots and cavalry and buried with the rites due a duke.'
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously name him general of chariots and cavalry and bury him with ducal honors.'

sentences.zh: 」谥曰贞侯。

translations.literal: (Close of prior imperial edict.) He was given the posthumous title Marquis Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: The preceding rescript ended; the court then canonized him as Marquis Zhen.

sentences.zh: 子钦嗣。

translations.literal: His son Qin succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xu Qin inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 卫臻字公振，陳留襄邑人也。

translations.literal: Wei Zhen, courtesy name Gongzhen, was a native of Xiangyi in Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhen, style Gongzhen, came from Xiangyi in Chenliu commandery.

sentences.zh: 父兹，有大节，不應三公之辟。

translations.literal: His father Ci possessed great integrity and did not answer summons from the three excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wei Ci held fast to principle and ignored every offer from the three highest offices.

sentences.zh: 太祖之初至陳留，兹曰：「平天下者，必此人也。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor first reached Chenliu, Ci said, 'The one who will pacify the realm must be this man.'
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao first entered Chenliu, Wei Ci declared, 'This is the man who will settle the empire.'

sentences.zh: 」太祖亦異之，數詣兹议大事。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor also marveled at him and repeatedly visited Ci to deliberate great affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao was struck with admiration and called on him again and again to plan weighty matters.

sentences.zh: 從討董卓，戰于荥阳而卒。

translations.literal: He followed in the punitive expedition against Dong Zhuo, fought at Xingyang, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He marched against Dong Zhuo, fell fighting at Xingyang, and died there.

sentences.zh: 太祖每涉郡境，辄遣使祠焉。

translations.literal: Whenever the Grand Progenitor crossed the commandery's territory he would send envoys to sacrifice at Ci's grave.
translations.idiomatic: Each time Cao Cao passed through Chenliu he dispatched aides to honor Ci's tomb.

sentences.zh: 〈《先贤行状》曰：兹字子许。

translations.literal: The Conduct of Worthies of Antiquity states: Ci, courtesy name Zixu.
translations.idiomatic: The Conduct of Worthies of Antiquity gives Ci's style as Zixu.

sentences.zh: 不为激诡之行，不徇流俗之名；

translations.literal: He did not perform sensational or devious acts, nor did he pursue the names fashionable in vulgar society.
translations.idiomatic: He shunned theatrical virtue and the empty reputations of the crowd.

sentences.zh: 明虑渊深，规略宏远。

translations.literal: His clear thought was deep as an abyss; his plans and strategies were vast and far-reaching.
translations.idiomatic: His mind ran deep; his designs ranged far.

sentences.zh: 为车骑将军何苗所辟，司徒杨彪再加旌命。

translations.literal: He was summoned by General of Chariots and Cavalry He Miao, and Minister of Education Yang Biao twice extended him decorated appointment.
translations.idiomatic: He Miao of the chariots and horse host called him up; Yang Biao, minister of education, twice pressed a grand summons on him.

sentences.zh: 董卓作乱，汉室倾荡，太祖到陈留，始与兹相见，遂同盟，计兴武事。

translations.literal: When Dong Zhuo threw the court into chaos and the house of Han tottered, the Grand Progenitor arrived at Chenliu, first met Ci, and thereupon formed an alliance with him to plan the raising of arms.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuo wrecked Luoyang and Han swayed, Cao Cao reached Chenliu, met Wei Ci, swore common cause, and plotted the uprising.

sentences.zh: 兹答曰：“乱生久矣，非兵无以整之。

translations.literal: Ci answered, 'Disorder has lasted long; without arms there is no way to set it right.'
translations.idiomatic: Ci replied, 'Chaos has festered too long—only force can mend it.'

sentences.zh: ”且言“兵之兴者，自今始矣”。

translations.literal: He added the words, 'The raising of arms begins from this day.'
translations.idiomatic: He added, 'This day marks the true beginning of the sword.'

sentences.zh: 深见废兴，首赞弘谋。

translations.literal: He deeply grasped rise and fall and was first to endorse the great design.
translations.idiomatic: He read the tides of fortune and was the first to bless the grand strategy.

sentences.zh: 合兵三千人，从太祖入荥阳，力战终日，失利，身殁。

translations.literal: He gathered three thousand soldiers, followed the Grand Progenitor into Xingyang, fought bitterly all day, met defeat, and perished in the field.
translations.idiomatic: He raised three thousand men, followed Cao Cao into Xingyang, battled a full day in defeat, and died on the field.

sentences.zh: 郭林宗传曰：“兹弱冠与同郡圈文生俱称盛德。

translations.literal: Guo Linzong's biography states: 'In his youth Ci, together with Quan Wensheng of the same commandery, was praised for lofty virtue.'
translations.idiomatic: Guo Tai's life records that in early manhood Ci and his townsman Quan Wensheng shared a reputation for high character.'

sentences.zh: 林宗与二人共至市，子许买物，随价雠直，文生訾呵，减价乃取。

translations.literal: Linzong went with the two to market: Zixu bought goods, paying whatever price was asked; Wensheng haggled and would take only after the price was lowered.
translations.idiomatic: At market with Guo Tai, Zixu paid the sticker price while Wensheng wrangled every copper lower.

sentences.zh: 林宗曰：“子许少欲，文生多情，此二人非徒兄弟，乃父子也。

translations.literal: Linzong said, 'Zixu has few desires, Wensheng many passions—these two are not merely brothers, they are father and son in temperament.'
translations.idiomatic: Guo Tai remarked, 'Zixu wants little; Wensheng wants much—they are less like brothers than like father and son.'

sentences.zh: ”后文生以秽货见损，兹以烈节垂名。〉

translations.literal: Later Wensheng was ruined by ill-gotten goods, while Ci won lasting fame through fierce integrity.'〉
translations.idiomatic: Wensheng later fell to greed; Ci's stern honor became legend.' (End of note.)

sentences.zh: 夏侯惇爲陳留太守，舉臻计吏，命妇出宴，臻以爲「末世之俗，非礼之正」。

translations.literal: When Xiahou Dun was grand warden of Chenliu he recommended Zhen as counting clerk and ordered the womenfolk to come out for a banquet; Zhen held that 'this is the custom of a decadent age, not the correctness of ritual.'
translations.idiomatic: Xiahou Dun nominated him counting clerk and ordered wives to attend a feast; Zhen protested that such mixing was decadent, not canonical.

sentences.zh: 惇怒，执臻，既而赦之。

translations.literal: Dun grew angry and seized Zhen, then afterward pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Dun jailed him in a fury, then thought better of it and let him go.

sentences.zh: 後爲汉黄门侍郎。

translations.literal: Later he became gentleman at the yellow gates of Han.
translations.idiomatic: He later served the Han court as gentleman at the yellow gates.

sentences.zh: 东郡硃越謀反，引臻。

translations.literal: Zhu Yue of Dongjun plotted rebellion and implicated Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Yue of Dongjun rebelled he tried to drag Zhen in.

sentences.zh: 太祖令曰：「孤與卿君同共舉事，加钦令问。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor issued an order saying, 'I and your father together raised this enterprise, and I hold you, sir, in added regard.'
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao wrote, 'Your father and I began this venture together, and I have watched you with special favor.'

sentences.zh: 始聞越言，固自不信。

translations.literal: When I first heard Yue's words I naturally did not believe them.
translations.idiomatic: When I first heard Yue's tale I did not credit it.

sentences.zh: 及得荀令君書，具亮忠诚。

translations.literal: When I received Director Xun's letter, your whole-hearted loyalty shone clear.'
translations.idiomatic: Director Xun's letter then proved your innocence to the hilt.'

sentences.zh: 」會奉诏命，聘贵人于魏，因表留臻参丞相軍事。

translations.literal: It happened that he received an imperial mandate to escort an honored consort to Wei, and on that basis memorialized to retain Zhen as staff to the chancellor's military bureau.
translations.idiomatic: On mission to invest a consort in Wei, he memorialized to keep Zhen on the chancellor's military staff.

sentences.zh: 追录臻父旧勋，赐爵關内侯，转爲户曹掾。

translations.literal: Tracing Zhen's father's old merit, the court granted him secondary marquis within the passes and transferred him to clerk of the households bureau.
translations.idiomatic: The throne remembered his father's service, enfeoffed him secondary marquis within the passes, and moved him to the households bureau.

sentences.zh: 文帝即王位，爲散骑常侍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen assumed the kingly title Zhen became standing attendant-in-ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: When Wendi took the kingship Zhen became standing attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 及践阼，封安國亭侯。

translations.literal: When he ascended the throne Zhen was enfeoffed as village marquis of Anguo.
translations.idiomatic: At Wendi's accession he was named village marquis of Anguo.

sentences.zh: 時羣臣并颂魏德，多抑损前朝。

translations.literal: At that time the assembled ministers together praised Wei's virtue and for the most part belittled the former dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: The whole court sang Wei's praises and slighted the fallen Han.

sentences.zh: 臻獨明禅授之義，称扬汉美。

translations.literal: Zhen alone clarified the meaning of abdication by transmission of the mandate and extolled Han's excellence.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen alone explained the doctrine of sanctioned transfer and spoke well of Han.

sentences.zh: 帝數目臻曰：「天下之珍，当與山阳共之。

translations.literal: The emperor repeatedly glanced at Zhen and said, 'The treasures of the realm ought to be shared with Shanyang.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor kept his eye on Zhen and said, 'The empire's jewels belong beside the lord of Shanyang too.'

sentences.zh: 」遷尚書，转侍中吏部尚書。

translations.literal: He was promoted to the Masters of Writing, then rotated to palace attendant and director of the Masters of Writing for personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to the Masters of Writing, then combined palace attendant with director for appointments.

sentences.zh: 帝幸广陵，行中领軍，從。

translations.literal: When the emperor visited Guangling Zhen acted as central commandant in his absence and accompanied him.
translations.idiomatic: During the Guangling tour he served as acting central commandant in the rear and rode with the train.

sentences.zh: 征軍大將軍曹休表得降贼辭，「孫权已在濡须口」。

translations.literal: General-in-chief for expeditions Cao Xiu submitted a memorial citing surrendered bandits' testimony that 'Sun Quan is already at Ruxukou.'
translations.idiomatic: Cao Xiu's memorial quoted prisoners swearing that Sun Quan had reached Ruxukou.

sentences.zh: 臻曰：「权恃長江，未敢抗衡，此必畏怖伪辭耳。

translations.literal: Zhen said, 'Quan relies on the Long River and does not dare meet us head-on—this must be frightened fabrications.'
translations.idiomatic: Zhen answered, 'Sun Quan hides behind the Yangzi; he would not dare a stand-up fight—this is panic talk.'

sentences.zh: 」考核降者，果守將诈所作也。

translations.literal: When the surrendered men were examined it proved to be a ruse forged by the defending commander.
translations.idiomatic: Questioning the captives exposed a lie cooked up by a local commander.

sentences.zh: 明帝即位，进封康鄉侯，後转爲右仆射，典選舉，如前加侍中。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming took the throne Zhen's fief was advanced to village marquis of Kang; later he rotated to right vice-director, in charge of appointments as before with added palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Mingdi raised his fief to village marquis of Kang, then made him right vice-director of personnel with palace attendant as before.

sentences.zh: 中护軍蒋济遺臻書曰：「汉祖遇亡虏爲上將，周武拔渔父爲太师；

translations.literal: Central protector Jiang Ji sent Zhen a letter saying, 'Han Gaozu made a fugitive slave his chief general, King Wu of Zhou raised a fisherman to grand tutor;
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Ji wrote, 'Gaozu turned a runaway groom into a marshal; the Zhou king made a fisherman grand tutor;

sentences.zh: 布衣厮养，可登王公，何必守文，试而後用？

translations.literal: men in plain cloth and stable grooms can mount to duke and king—why must one cling to written precedent and try only after testing?'
translations.idiomatic: commoners and grooms can rise to the highest rank—why fetishize paperwork and probation?'

sentences.zh: 」臻答曰：「古人遺智慧而任度量，须考绩而加黜陟；

translations.literal: Zhen answered, 'The ancients left wisdom aside and trusted measure; they waited for performance review before promoting or demoting;
translations.idiomatic: Zhen replied, 'The sages weighed deed over dazzle and moved men only after reviewing their record;

sentences.zh: 今子同牧野於成、康，喻断蛇於文、景，好不经之舉，开拔奇之津，將使天下驰骋而起矣。

translations.literal: now you, sir, liken the fields of Muye to the eras of Cheng and Kang, compare the severed snake omen to the reigns of Wen and Jing, delight in irregular leaps, and open a ford for pulling up odd talents—you will set the realm galloping without rein.'
translations.idiomatic: yet you compare Muye to the peace of Cheng and Kang, equate a street omen with Wen and Jing, praise reckless jumps, and open a sluice for eccentric talent—the whole country will career off the road.'

sentences.zh: 」諸葛亮寇天水，臻奏：「宜遣奇兵入散關，绝其粮道。

translations.literal: When Zhuge Liang raided Tianshui Zhen memorialized, 'It is fitting to dispatch a striking column through Sanguan to cut his grain road.'
translations.idiomatic: When Liang struck Tianshui Zhen urged a flying column through Sanguan to sever his supplies.

sentences.zh: 」乃以臻爲征蜀將軍，假节督諸軍事，到長安，亮退。

translations.literal: Thereupon Zhen was appointed general for the Shu expedition, granted the staff of authority, and placed in command of all military affairs; he reached Chang'an, and Liang withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The court named him Shu-expedition general with the credential staff, sent him to Chang'an, and Liang pulled back.

sentences.zh: 還，复职，加光禄大夫。

translations.literal: On return he resumed his former duties and was given the additional title grand master for splendid happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to civil office and added grand master for splendid happiness.

sentences.zh: 是時，帝方隆意於殿舍，臻數切諫。

translations.literal: At this time the emperor was pouring his heart into palace halls, and Zhen remonstrated sharply several times.
translations.idiomatic: While Mingdi lavished treasure on new palaces, Zhen remonstrated again and again.

sentences.zh: 及殿中监擅收兰台令史，臻奏案之。

translations.literal: When the palace intendant on his own authority arrested a clerk of the Orchid Terrace, Zhen submitted a memorial impeaching the case.
translations.idiomatic: When the palace intendant seized an Orchid Terrace clerk without warrant, Zhen impeached the abuse.

sentences.zh: 诏曰：「殿舍不成，吾所留心，卿推之何？

translations.literal: An edict said, 'The palace halls are not yet finished—this is what engages my mind; why do you press this?'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, 'My mind is on the unfinished halls—why do you harp on this?'

sentences.zh: 」臻上疏曰：「古制侵官之法，非恶其勤事也，诚以所益者小，所堕者大也。

translations.literal: Zhen submitted a memorial saying, 'The ancient statutes against encroaching on another office's authority did not hate diligent service—they truly reckoned that the gain was small while the harm was great.'
translations.idiomatic: Zhen answered, 'Old law forbade officials poaching one another's duties not because diligence was bad but because the profit was tiny and the damage huge.'

sentences.zh: 臣每察校事，類皆如此，惧羣司將遂越职，以至陵迟矣。

translations.literal: Your subject each time investigates such supervisory cases and finds them mostly thus; I fear the bureaus will overstep their posts until standards collapse.'
translations.idiomatic: Every time I review such cases I see the same pattern—I dread a race of clerks trampling each other's lines until government rots.'

sentences.zh: 」亮又出斜谷；

translations.literal: Liang again issued forth from Xie Valley;
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang marched out of Xie Valley again;

sentences.zh: 征南上：「硃然等軍已过荆城。

translations.literal: the southern expedition reported, 'Zhu Ran and others have already passed Jingcheng.'
translations.idiomatic: the southern front reported, 'Zhu Ran's fleet has passed Jingcheng.'

sentences.zh: 」臻曰：「然，吴之骁將，必下從权，且爲勢以缀征南耳。

translations.literal: Zhen said, 'Ran is a fierce general of Wu; he is sure to descend to follow Quan and merely feints to tie down the southern expedition.'
translations.idiomatic: Zhen said, 'Zhu Ran is one of Wu's best blades—he will join Quan in person and only feints to pin our southern army.'

sentences.zh: 」权果召然入居巢，进攻合肥。

translations.literal: Quan indeed summoned Ran to enter Juchao and attack Hefei.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan did recall Zhu Ran to Juchao and strike at Hefei.

sentences.zh: 帝欲自东征，臻曰：「权外示應亮，内实观望。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to campaign east in person; Zhen said, 'Quan outwardly shows he answers Liang but inwardly watches and waits.
translations.idiomatic: Mingdi meant to lead the eastern host himself; Zhen argued, 'Sun Quan pretends to help Liang but actually waits on the fence.'

sentences.zh: 且合肥城固，不足爲虑。

translations.literal: Moreover Hefei's walls are strong—not a matter for worry.
translations.idiomatic: Hefei's ramparts are stout—hardly a crisis.'

sentences.zh: 车驾可无亲征，以省六軍之费。

translations.literal: The imperial train need not go in person, so as to save the expense of the six armies.'
translations.idiomatic: Spare the six hosts the cost of a needless imperial march.'

sentences.zh: 」帝到寻阳而权竟退。

translations.literal: The emperor reached Xunyang, and Quan in the end withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign advanced only to Xunyang; Sun Quan slipped away.

sentences.zh: 子烈嗣，咸熙中爲光禄勋。

translations.literal: His son Lie succeeded; in the Xianxi era he became superintendent of the palace for splendid happiness.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wei Lie inherited the title and under Xianxi became superintendent of splendid happiness.

sentences.zh: 〈臣松之案旧事及《傅咸集》，烈终於光禄勋。

translations.literal: Your subject Songzhi notes that according to old records and Fu Xian's collected works, Lie ended his career as superintendent of splendid happiness.
translations.idiomatic: Songzhi: old files and Fu Xian's corpus agree that Wei Lie died in office as superintendent of splendid happiness.

sentences.zh: 烈二弟京、楷，皆二千石。

translations.literal: Lie had two younger brothers, Jing and Kai, both of whom reached two-thousand-dan rank.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's younger brothers Jing and Kai each rose to two-thousand-dan posts.

sentences.zh: 楷子權，字伯舆。

translations.literal: Kai's son Quan, courtesy name Boyu.
translations.idiomatic: Kai's son Quan bore the style Boyu.

sentences.zh: 晋大司马汝南王亮辅政，以权为尚书郎。

translations.literal: When grand marshal Prince Liang of Runan assisted the government of Jin, he appointed Quan gentleman of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Liang of Runan, grand marshal of Jin, directed the regency, he named Quan gentleman of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 傅咸与亮笺曰：“卫伯舆贵妃兄子，诚有才章，应作台郎，然未得东宫官属。

translations.literal: Fu Xian wrote Prince Liang a note saying, 'Wei Boyu is the nephew of a honored consort's brother—he truly has literary talent and ought to serve as a terrace gentleman, yet he has not yet received an eastern-palace post.'
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xian warned the prince, 'Wei Quan is kin to the imperial consort and has real literary gifts—he belongs on the terrace staff, not yet in the heir's bureau.'

sentences.zh: 东宫官属，前患杨骏，亲理塞路，今有伯舆，复越某作郎。

translations.literal: Eastern-palace posts previously suffered from Yang Jun's monopoly, blocking every path; now with Boyu another man vaults over me to become gentleman.'
translations.idiomatic: The heir's office once choked under Yang Jun's nepotism; now Quan leaps ahead of me for the same post.'

sentences.zh: 一犬吠形，群犬吠声，惧於群吠，遂至回听。

translations.literal: One dog barks at a shadow and the pack barks at the sound—I fear the pack's baying will twist what the ruler hears.'
translations.idiomatic: One cur barks at a shadow and a hundred echo—I dread the chorus warping the throne's ear.'

sentences.zh: ”权作左思《吴都赋》叙及注，叙粗有文辞，至於为注，了无所发明，直为尘秽纸墨，不合传写也。〉

translations.literal: Quan wrote the preface and commentary to Zuo Si's Rhapsody on the Wu Capital; the preface has some literary polish, but as for the commentary it illuminates nothing and is mere filth on paper and ink—not fit to be copied out.'〉
translations.idiomatic: Quan's preface and notes to Zuo Si's Wu Capital rhapsody show a little polish in the preface, but the commentary adds nothing—only smears the page and is not worth copying.'

sentences.zh: 卢毓字子家，涿郡涿人也。

translations.literal: Lu Yu, courtesy name Zijia, was a native of Zhuo in Zhuo commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yu, style Zijia, came from Zhuo in Zhuo commandery.

sentences.zh: 父植，有名於世。

translations.literal: His father Zhi was famous in the age.
translations.idiomatic: His father Lu Zhi was celebrated throughout the empire.

sentences.zh: 〈续汉书曰：植字子幹。

translations.literal: The Continued Han History states: Zhi, courtesy name Zigàn.
translations.idiomatic: The Xu Han shu records Lu Zhi's style as Zigàn.

sentences.zh: 少事马融，与郑玄同门相友。

translations.literal: In youth he studied under Ma Zheng and was a fellow student and friend of Zheng Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he studied under Ma Rong alongside Zheng Xuan.

sentences.zh: 植刚毅有大节，常喟然有济世之志，不苟合取容，不应州郡命召。

translations.literal: Zhi was stern and resolute with great integrity; he often sighed with the ambition to aid the age, would not compromise to win favor, and did not answer summons from provinces or commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi was granite-straight, dreamed of saving the world, refused to curry favor, and ignored provincial calls.

sentences.zh: 建宁中，徵博士，出补九江太守，以病去官。

translations.literal: In the Jianning era he was summoned as erudite, went out to fill the post of grand warden of Jiujiang, and left office because of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jianning he took a doctorate, became grand warden of Jiujiang, then resigned ill.

sentences.zh: 作尚书章句、礼记解诂。

translations.literal: He composed chapter-and-verse glosses on the Documents and exegesis on the Record of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote a commentary on the Documents and glosses on the Record of Rites.

sentences.zh: 稍迁侍中、尚书。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to palace attendant and masters of writing.
translations.idiomatic: He rose step by step to palace attendant and the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 张角起，以植为北中郎将征角，失利抵罪。

translations.literal: When Zhang Jue rose, Zhi was appointed colonel of the central north to campaign against Jue, met defeat, and was liable to punishment.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Jue rebelled the court named him colonel of the central north; he lost and faced trial.

sentences.zh: 顷之，复以为尚书。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was again appointed to the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was restored to the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 张让劫少帝奔小平津，植手剑责数让等，让等皆放兵，垂泣谢罪，遂自杀。

translations.literal: When Zhang Rang seized the young emperor and fled to Little Ping Ford, Zhi, sword in hand, rebuked Rang and his party; they all lowered their weapons, wept, and begged forgiveness, whereupon they committed suicide.
translations.idiomatic: At Little Ping Ford Lu Zhi confronted Zhang Rang's party with drawn blade until the eunuchs disarmed, wept, and begged mercy—then they killed themselves.

sentences.zh: 董卓议欲废帝，众莫敢对，植独正言，语在《卓传》。

translations.literal: When Dong Zhuo debated deposing the emperor none dared answer save Zhi, who spoke straight—the account is in Zhuo's biography.
translations.idiomatic: At Zhuo's council to depose the throne only Lu Zhi spoke bluntly—the story stands in Zhuo's chapter.

sentences.zh: 植以老病去位，隐居上谷军都山，初平三年卒。

translations.literal: Zhi left office because of age and illness, retired to Mount Jundu in Shanggu, and died in the third year of Chuping.
translations.idiomatic: Age and sickness drove him to hermitage on Mount Jundu in Shanggu; he died in Chuping 3.

sentences.zh: 太祖北征柳城，过涿郡，令告太守曰：“故北中郎将卢植，名著海内，学为儒宗，士之楷模，乃国之桢幹也。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor campaigned north to Liucheng and passed through Zhuo commandery he ordered the grand warden to be told, 'The late colonel of the central north Lu Zhi, whose name resounded within the seas, whose learning was patriarch of the ru, model for gentlemen, was a pillar of the state.'
translations.idiomatic: Marching on Liucheng Cao Cao told Zhuo's grand warden, 'Lu Zhi, late colonel of the central north, was Confucianism's beacon and the state's beam—his fame filled the realm.'

sentences.zh: 昔武王入殷，封商容之闾，郑丧子产而仲尼陨涕。

translations.literal: Long ago King Wu entered Yin and ennobled Shang Rong's lane; when Zheng lost Zi Chan Confucius wept tears.
translations.idiomatic: King Wu of Zhou honored Shang Rong's lane in conquered Yin; Confucius wept when Zi Chan died in Zheng.'

sentences.zh: 孤到此州，嘉其餘风。

translations.literal: I, alone, coming to this commandery, admire the lingering influence he left.
translations.idiomatic: Coming to his home commandery, I honor the virtue that still clings here.'

sentences.zh: 春秋之义，贤者之后，有异於人。

translations.literal: By the principle of the Spring and Autumn, the posterity of the worthy is to be treated differently from others.
translations.idiomatic: Spring and Autumn justice demands special kindness to descendants of the worthy.'

sentences.zh: 敬遣丞掾脩坟墓，并致薄醊，以彰厥德。

translations.literal: Respectfully I send assistants to repair his tomb mound and offer modest libations, so as to make manifest his virtue.'
translations.idiomatic: I therefore send clerks to tend his grave and pour a humble libation, that his goodness may shine.'

sentences.zh: ”植有四子，毓最小。〉

translations.literal: Zhi had four sons; Yu was the youngest.'〉
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi left four sons; Yu was the youngest.' (End of note.)

sentences.zh: 毓十岁而孤，遇本州乱，二兄死難。

translations.literal: Yu was orphaned at ten sui; encountering rebellion in his province, his two elder brothers died in the crisis.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned at ten when his province exploded in war, he lost both elder brothers in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 当袁紹、公孫瓚交兵，幽冀饥荒，养寡嫂孤兄子，以学行见称。

translations.literal: When Yuan Shao and Gongsun Zan crossed arms, You and Ji knew famine; he raised his widowed sister-in-law and his elder brothers' orphaned sons and was praised for learning and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shao–Zan wars that starved You and Ji he kept his sister-in-law and nephews alive and won praise for scholarship and character.

sentences.zh: 文帝爲五官將，召毓署门下贼曹。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen was general of the five offices he summoned Yu to serve as clerk of the gatehouse bandit bureau.
translations.idiomatic: As general of the five offices Wendi appointed him clerk of the gatehouse bandit bureau.

sentences.zh: 崔琰舉爲冀州主簿。

translations.literal: Cui Yan recommended him as chief clerk of Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yan nominated him chief clerk of Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 時天下草创，多逋逃，故重士亡法，罪及妻子。

translations.literal: At that time the realm was newly founded and many fled their obligations; therefore the law on fugitive gentlemen was strict, extending guilt to wives and children.
translations.idiomatic: Early Wei punished runaway officials harshly, extending sentence to wives and children.

sentences.zh: 亡士妻白等，始適夫家數日，未與夫相见，大理奏弃巿。

translations.literal: The wives of fugitives, such as Bai, had only just entered their husbands' houses for several days and had not yet met their husbands; the court of great reason memorialized for execution in the market.
translations.idiomatic: Women such as Bai had been wed mere days and never seen their husbands when the high court demanded public execution.

sentences.zh: 毓驳之曰：

translations.literal: Yu objected, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Yu protested:

sentences.zh: 夫女子之情，以接见而恩生，成妇而義重。

translations.literal: As for the feelings of women, affection arises from meeting in person, and duty grows weighty once she becomes wife.
translations.idiomatic: A woman's bond forms at first sight of her husband; duty deepens only after the marriage is complete.

sentences.zh: 故诗云‘未见君子，我心伤悲；

translations.literal: Therefore the Odes says, 'I have not seen my lord; my heart is wounded with sorrow;
translations.idiomatic: The Poetry says, 'I have not seen my lord, and sorrow wrenches my heart;

sentences.zh: 亦既见止，我心則夷’。

translations.literal: now that I have seen him, my heart is then at peace.'
translations.idiomatic: now that I have seen him, my heart is eased.'

sentences.zh: 又礼‘未庙见之妇而死，归葬女氏之黨，以未成妇也’。

translations.literal: Moreover the Rites states, 'If a woman who has not yet been presented in the ancestral temple dies, she is returned for burial to her mother's kin, because she has not yet completed being a wife.'
translations.idiomatic: The canon adds, 'A bride not yet presented at the temple who dies goes home to her mother's clan, for she is not yet truly a wife.'

sentences.zh: 今白等生有未见之悲，死有非妇之痛，而吏议欲肆之大辟，則若同牢合卺之後，罪何所加？

translations.literal: Now Bai and the others had in life the grief of never having seen their husbands, in death the pain of not being wives, yet clerical opinion wished to apply to them the extreme punishment of rending—then if it were after sharing the marriage couch and the nuptial cup, to what crime could further guilt be added?
translations.idiomatic: These women knew their husbands only by rumor in life and died without ever completing a marriage, yet the tribunal would execute them—had they truly shared a bed, what worse charge could you pile on?

sentences.zh: 且记曰‘附從轻’，言附人之罪，以轻者爲比也。

translations.literal: Moreover the Record states, 'Attach guilt by the lighter analogy,' meaning that when attaching guilt to another one takes the lighter case as comparison.
translations.idiomatic: The Record also says to grade complicity by the lightest plausible reading.

sentences.zh: 又書云‘與其杀不辜，宁失不经’，恐过重也。

translations.literal: Moreover the Documents says, 'Rather than kill the innocent, it is better to miss the irregular'—I fear this is too heavy.
translations.idiomatic: The Documents warns: better break precedent than kill the guiltless—your proposed sentence is too harsh.

sentences.zh: 苟以白等皆受礼聘，已入门庭，刑之爲可，杀之爲重。

translations.literal: If one grants that Bai and the others all received ritual betrothal and had already entered the gate and courtyard, to punish them may be acceptable, but to kill them is excessive.
translations.idiomatic: They had crossed the threshold under formal betrothal—fine them or demote them if you must, but the headsman's ax is excessive.

sentences.zh: 太祖曰：「毓执之是也。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor said, 'Yu holds to this correctly.'
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao ruled, 'Lu Yu has the right of it.'

sentences.zh: 又引经典有意，使孤叹息。

translations.literal: Moreover he cited the classics with clear intent, causing me, alone, to sigh.
translations.idiomatic: He grounded his plea in the canon until I could only sigh in agreement.

sentences.zh: 」由是爲丞相法曹议令史，转西曹议令史。

translations.literal: Thereupon he became deliberation clerk to the chancellor's legal bureau, then transferred to deliberation clerk of the western bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He was named deliberation clerk in the legal bureau, then rotated to the western bureau.

sentences.zh: 魏國既建，爲吏部郎。

translations.literal: When the state of Wei was established he became gentleman of the ministry of personnel.
translations.idiomatic: At Wei's founding he took office as gentleman of the ministry of personnel.

sentences.zh: 文帝践阼，徙黄门侍郎，出爲济阴相，梁、谯二郡太守。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen ascended the throne he was transferred to gentleman at the yellow gates, went out as minister of Jiyin, and grand warden of Liang and Qiao commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Wendi moved him to the yellow gates, then sent him out as Jiyin minister and joint grand warden of Liang and Qiao.

sentences.zh: 帝以谯旧鄉，故大徙民充之，以爲屯田。

translations.literal: Because Qiao was the emperor's old home, he therefore moved a great mass of people to fill it, intending to make colony fields.
translations.idiomatic: Because Qiao was the imperial hometown, Wendi transplanted a huge population there to open military colonies.

sentences.zh: 而谯土地墝瘠，百姓穷困，毓愍之，上表徙民於梁國就沃衍，失帝意。

translations.literal: Yet the soil of Qiao was barren and thin and the common people were destitute; Yu pitied them and submitted a memorial to move the settlers into the state of Liang where the land was rich and wide, missing the emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: The ground was poor and the settlers starving; Yu begged to shift them to fertile Liang state—Wendi took it as a snub.

sentences.zh: 雖听毓所表，心犹恨之，遂左遷毓，使將徙民爲睢阳典农校尉。

translations.literal: Although he followed Yu's memorial, in his heart he still resented it, and therefore demoted Yu, ordering him to lead the relocated people as colony commandant of Suiyang.
translations.idiomatic: He grudgingly approved the move yet exiled Yu to command the colonists as Suiyang colony commandant.

sentences.zh: 毓心在利民，躬自臨视，择居美田，百姓賴之。

translations.literal: Yu's mind was set on benefiting the people; he personally went to inspect, chose dwellings on fine fields, and the common people relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: Yu walked every camp himself, picking good soil for each family, and the people thrived under his hand.

sentences.zh: 遷安平、广平太守，所在有惠化。

translations.literal: He was promoted to grand warden of Anping and Guangping; wherever he served there was kind transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to grand warden of Anping and Guangping, he left a trail of humane government.

sentences.zh: 青龙二年，入爲侍中。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qinglong he entered the court as palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In Qinglong 2 he returned to the palace as attendant.

sentences.zh: 先是，散骑常侍劉劭受诏定律，未就。

translations.literal: Earlier, standing attendant-in-ordinary Liu Shao had received an edict to codify the laws, but it was not completed.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shao had been drafting a new code for the throne, but the work stalled.

sentences.zh: 毓上论古今科律之意，以爲法宜一正，不宜有两端，使奸吏得容情。

translations.literal: Yu submitted a discussion of the meaning of statutes old and new, holding that the law ought to be unified in rectitude and ought not to have two ends, enabling crafty clerks to harbor partiality.
translations.idiomatic: Yu argued that statutes must speak with one voice—split standards only feed corrupt clerks.

sentences.zh: 及侍中高堂隆數以宫室事切諫，帝不悦，毓进曰：「臣聞君明則臣直，古之圣王恐不聞其过，故有敢諫之鼓。

translations.literal: When Palace Attendant Gaotang Long repeatedly used the matter of palace halls to remonstrate sharply and the emperor was displeased, Yu advanced and said, 'Your subject has heard that when the ruler is enlightened the ministers are straight; the sage kings of antiquity feared not to hear their faults, and therefore had drums for daring remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaotang Long's palace sermons angered Mingdi, Yu stepped forward: 'A clear-sighted throne breeds blunt ministers; the ancients hung a drum so subjects could beat out their warnings.'

sentences.zh: 近臣尽規，此乃臣等所以不及隆。

translations.literal: That close ministers exhaust their remonstrance—this is why your subjects and the rest do not match Long.
translations.idiomatic: We lesser attendants cannot match Long's courage in speaking truth to power.'

sentences.zh: 隆諸生，名爲狂直，陛下宜容之。

translations.literal: Long is a classicist by training, styled madcap and blunt; Your Majesty ought to tolerate him.'
translations.idiomatic: He is a scholar, blunt to a fault—bear with him.'

sentences.zh: 」在职三年，多所驳争。

translations.literal: In office three years he refuted and contended on many matters.
translations.idiomatic: Three years in post he fought a dozen bad rulings.

sentences.zh: 诏曰：「官人秩才，圣帝所難，必须良佐，进可替否。

translations.literal: An edict said, 'To rank officials by talent is what even sage emperors find hard; one must have good assistants who advance the capable and replace the incapable.
translations.idiomatic: An edict admitted that matching men to rank stumps even sages and requires aides who promote the fit and retire the tired.'

sentences.zh: 侍中毓禀性贞固，心平体正，可謂明试有功，不懈于位者也。

translations.literal: Palace attendant Yu's endowment is chaste and firm, his heart level and his person straight—he may be called one who has clearly been tested and achieved merit, unwearied in his post.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Lu Yu is steady, fair, and tireless—exactly the man to test and trust.'

sentences.zh: 其以毓爲吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Let Yu be made director of the ministry of personnel.'
translations.idiomatic: Appoint him director of personnel.'

sentences.zh: 」使毓自選代，曰：「得如卿者乃可。

translations.literal: He ordered Yu to choose his own successor, saying, 'Only one like yourself will do.'
translations.idiomatic: Mingdi told him to name his successor: 'Only your equal will do.'

sentences.zh: 」毓舉常侍郑冲，帝曰：「文和，吾自知之，更舉吾所未聞者。

translations.literal: Yu nominated standing attendant Zheng Chong; the emperor said, 'Wenhe—I already know him; nominate another whom I have not heard of.'
translations.idiomatic: Yu picked Zheng Chong; the emperor answered, 'I know Wenhe—give me a name I have not met.'

sentences.zh: 」乃舉阮武、孫邕，帝於是用邕。

translations.literal: Thereupon he nominated Ruan Wu and Sun Yong, and the emperor thereupon employed Yong.
translations.idiomatic: He then offered Ruan Wu and Sun Yong; the throne took Sun Yong.

sentences.zh: 前此諸葛诞、邓飏等驰名誉，有四

translations.literal: Earlier Zhuge Dan, Deng Yang, and others had raced for reputation, earning the mocking label 'the four
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Dan, Deng Yang, and their set chased fame until the capital sneered at the 'four

translations.literal: (text: 窗, scribal variant for 聪)
translations.idiomatic: acute'—

sentences.zh: 八达之诮，帝疾之。

translations.literal: eight thoroughfares' wits,' and the emperor detested them.
translations.idiomatic: eight thoroughfares' clique,' and Mingdi detested them.

sentences.zh: 時舉中書郎，诏曰：「得其人與否，在卢生耳。

translations.literal: At that time they were selecting a gentleman of the palace secretariat; an edict said, 'Whether the right man is obtained lies with Master Lu.'
translations.idiomatic: When a palace secretariat seat opened, the edict read, 'Master Lu alone will tell us if the man fits.'

sentences.zh: 選舉莫取有名，名如画地作饼，不可啖也。

translations.literal: In selection do not take men merely because they are famous; fame is like drawing a cake on the ground—it cannot be eaten.'
translations.idiomatic: Do not pick men for fame alone—fame is a cake drawn in dust, inedible.'

sentences.zh: 」毓对曰：

translations.literal: Yu replied:
translations.idiomatic: Yu answered:

sentences.zh: 名不足以致異人，而可以得常士。

translations.literal: A name is not enough to obtain extraordinary men, yet it can obtain ordinary gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: Reputation alone will not net a genius, but it still finds solid middling talent.

sentences.zh: 常士畏教慕善，然後有名，非所当疾也。

translations.literal: Ordinary gentlemen fear instruction and admire goodness; only afterward do they have a name—this is not what ought to be detested.
translations.idiomatic: Reliable men heed teaching and earn their names honestly—that is nothing to despise.'

sentences.zh: 愚臣既不足以识異人，又主者正以循名案常爲职，但当有以验其後。
