translations.literal: Your foolish subject is insufficient to recognize extraordinary men, moreover those in charge take following names and investigating the routine as their duty—only there ought to be means to verify their subsequent performance.
translations.idiomatic: I cannot spot every prodigy, and my clerks must work from dossiers—yet we can still test results after appointment.'

sentences.zh: 故古者敷奏以言，明试以功。

translations.literal: Therefore in antiquity they spread memorials in words and clearly tested by achievement.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients heard memorials in court and proved officers on the job.'

sentences.zh: 今考绩之法废，而以毁誉相进退，故真伪浑杂，虚实相蒙。

translations.literal: Now the law of performance review is abandoned, while advancement and demotion follow slander and praise—therefore true and false are mixed in confusion, substance and emptiness veil each other.
translations.idiomatic: Today merit ratings are dead and gossip sets promotions—so fraud and fact tangle together.'

sentences.zh: 帝納其言，即诏作考课法。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted his words and immediately ordered the drafting of a performance-review law.
translations.idiomatic: Mingdi accepted the plea and ordered a new examination code drafted.

sentences.zh: 會司徒缺，毓舉处士管宁，帝不能用。

translations.literal: It happened that the minister of education was vacant; Yu nominated recluse Guan Ning, but the emperor could not employ him.
translations.idiomatic: When the minister of education's chair emptied, Yu nominated Guan Ning; the court could not use him.

sentences.zh: 更问其次，毓对曰：「敦笃至行，則太中大夫韩暨；

translations.literal: He was asked for the next choice, and Yu replied, 'For honest depth and consummate conduct, then grand counselor of the household Han Ji;
translations.idiomatic: Pressed for another name he answered, 'For generous steadfastness name grand counselor of the household Han Ji;

sentences.zh: 亮直清方，則司隶校尉崔林；

translations.literal: for brightness and straightness with pure standards, then metropolitan commandant Cui Lin;
translations.idiomatic: for blunt clarity name metropolitan commandant Cui Lin;

sentences.zh: 贞固纯粹，則太常常林。

translations.literal: for chaste firmness and pure simplicity, then grand master of ceremonies Chang Lin.'
translations.idiomatic: for unbending purity name grand master of ceremonies Chang Lin.'

sentences.zh: 」帝乃用暨。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon employed Han Ji.
translations.idiomatic: The throne named Han Ji to the post.

sentences.zh: 毓於人及選舉，先舉性行，而後言才。

translations.literal: In judging men and in selection Yu always advanced native character and conduct first and afterward spoke of talent.
translations.idiomatic: In every nomination Yu ranked character ahead of cleverness.

sentences.zh: 黄门李丰尝以问毓，毓曰：「才所以爲善也，故大才成大善，小才成小善。

translations.literal: Yellow-gate Li Feng once questioned Yu about this, and Yu said, 'Talent exists in order to accomplish goodness; therefore great talent completes great goodness and small talent completes small goodness.
translations.idiomatic: Li Feng asked how talent and virtue meshed; Yu said, 'Talent serves goodness—great gifts do great good, modest gifts do modest good.'

sentences.zh: 今称之有才而不能爲善，是才不中器也。

translations.literal: Now those praised as having talent yet unable to accomplish goodness are talents that do not fit their vessels.'
translations.idiomatic: Call a man clever who does no good and you have a misshapen vessel.'

sentences.zh: 」丰等服其言。

translations.literal: Feng and the others submitted to his words.
translations.idiomatic: Li Feng and his circle conceded the point.

sentences.zh: 毓子钦、珽，咸熙中钦爲尚書，珽泰山太守。

translations.literal: Yu's sons were Qin and Ting; in the Xianxi era Qin was in the Masters of Writing and Ting was grand warden of Taishan.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Lu Qin and Lu Ting rose under Xianxi—Qin to the Masters of Writing, Ting to grand warden of Taishan.

sentences.zh: 〈《世语》曰：钦字子若，珽字子笏。

translations.literal: The Shiyu states: Qin, courtesy name Ziruo; Ting, courtesy name Zihu.
translations.idiomatic: The Shiyu records Qin's style as Ziruo and Ting's as Zihu.

sentences.zh: 钦泰始中为尚书仆射，领选，咸宁四年卒，追赠卫将军，开府。

translations.literal: Under Taishi Qin became vice-director of the Masters of Writing with charge of appointments; he died in the fourth year of Xianning and was posthumously honored as guards general with establishment of a staff.'
translations.idiomatic: In Jin's Taishi era Qin served as vice-director of personnel; he died in Xianning 4 with posthumous rank as guards general and independent staff.'

sentences.zh: 《虞预晋书》曰：钦少居名位，不顾财利，清虚淡泊，动脩礼典。

translations.literal: Yu Yu's Jin History states: Qin from youth held name and office, did not care for wealth or profit, was clear, empty, and plain, and in movement cultivated ritual canons.
translations.idiomatic: In his Jin History Yu Yu records that Qin spurned riches, lived plainly, and shaped his life by ritual.

sentences.zh: 同郡张华，家单少孤，不为乡邑所知，惟钦贵异焉。

translations.literal: Zhang Hua of the same commandery, his family solitary and orphaned in youth, was unknown to town and village; only Qin honored him as extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: His townsman Zhang Hua was poor and obscure; only Qin singled him out as exceptional.

sentences.zh: 钦子浮，字子云。

translations.literal: Qin's son was Fu, courtesy name Ziyun.
translations.idiomatic: Qin's son Fu bore the style Ziyun.

sentences.zh: 《晋诸公赞》曰：张华博识多闻，无物不知。

translations.literal: The Jin Praise of the Dukes states: Zhang Hua was broadly learned and heard much; there was nothing he did not know.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin Praise of the Dukes calls Zhang Hua encyclopedic.

sentences.zh: 浮高朗经博，有美於华，起家太子舍人，病疽，截手，遂废。

translations.literal: Fu was high, clear, classical, and broad, with excellence surpassing Hua; he began office as attendant to the heir apparent, but when a boil illness required cutting off his hand he was thereafter disabled.
translations.idiomatic: Fu outshone even Zhang Hua in breadth, entered service as heir's attendant, then lost a hand to a boil and was crippled out of office.

sentences.zh: 朝廷器重之，就家以为国子博士，迁祭酒。

translations.literal: The court esteemed him and at his home appointed him erudite of the national university, then promoted him to libationer.
translations.idiomatic: The court still valued him, named him national-university erudite without leaving his house, then libationer.

sentences.zh: 永平中为秘书监。

translations.literal: In the Yongping era he became supervisor of the secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yongping he rose to supervisor of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 珽及子皓、志并至尚书。

translations.literal: Ting and his sons Hao and Zhi all reached the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ting and his sons Hao and Zhi each rose to the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 志子谌，字子谅。

translations.literal: Zhi's son was Chen, courtesy name Ziliang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi's son Chen used the style Ziliang.

sentences.zh: 温峤表称谌清出有文思。

translations.literal: Wen Qiao's memorial praised Chen as pure in emergence and possessed of literary thought.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Qiao memorialized that Chen combined moral clarity with literary grace.

sentences.zh: 《谌别传》曰：谌善著文章。

translations.literal: Chen's separate biography states: Chen was skilled at composing essays.
translations.idiomatic: A private biography of Chen praises his essays.

sentences.zh: 洛阳倾覆，北投刘琨，琨以为司空从事中郎。

translations.literal: When Luoyang collapsed he fled north to Liu Kun, and Kun made him staff adviser to the minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: When Luoyang fell he fled to Liu Kun, who named him minister of works staff adviser.

sentences.zh: 琨败，谌归段末波。

translations.literal: When Kun was defeated Chen returned to Duan Mobo.
translations.idiomatic: After Kun's defeat he entered the service of Duan Mobo.

sentences.zh: 元帝之初，累召为散骑中书侍郎，不得南赴。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuan Di's reign he was repeatedly summoned as standing attendant and gentleman of the palace secretariat but could not go south to answer.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yuan Di he was summoned again and again to the secretariat but could not cross south.

sentences.zh: 永和六年，卒於胡

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yonghe he died among the Hu
translations.idiomatic: In Yonghe 6 he died on soil held by the Hu

translations.literal: (Hu)
translations.idiomatic: the manuscripts repeat the ethnonym Hu in parentheses

sentences.zh: 中，子孙过江。

translations.literal: interior; his descendants crossed the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: while his descendants later crossed the Yangzi to the south.

sentences.zh: 妖贼帅卢循，谌之曾孙。〉

translations.literal: The sorcerer-rebel captain Lu Xun was Chen's great-grandson.'〉
translations.idiomatic: The rebel prophet Lu Xun was his great-grandson.' (End of note.)

translations.literal: Rubric heading: Appraisal.
translations.idiomatic: Section heading: Appraisal.

sentences.zh: 评曰：桓階识睹成敗，才周当世。

translations.literal: The appraisal states: Huan Jie discerned success and failure and his talent encompassed the age.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Jie read every turn of fortune and had the breadth to master his times.

sentences.zh: 陳羣动仗名義，有清流雅望；

translations.literal: Chen Qun in action relied on name and right principle and possessed the pure current and elegant reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Qun anchored policy in principle and kept a statesman's clean reputation.

sentences.zh: 泰弘济简至，允克堂构矣。

translations.literal: Tai broadly aided with cutting clarity and truly matched the hall's frame.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Tai carried the house forward with blunt, saving judgment.

sentences.zh: 魏世事统台阁，重内轻外，故八座尚書，即古六卿之任也。

translations.literal: Wei-era government unified the terrace and pavilion, esteeming the inner and slighting the outer; therefore the eight seats of the Masters of Writing were the charge of the ancient six ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Wei centralized power in the palace secretariat, favoring capital ministers over field posts—the eight seats of the Masters of Writing were the true heirs of the Zhou six ministers.

sentences.zh: 陳、徐、卫、卢，久居斯位，矫、宣剛断骨鲠，臻、毓規鉴清理，咸不忝厥职云。

translations.literal: Chen, Xu, Wei, and Lu long occupied these posts; Jiao and Xuan were resolute and unbending to the bone, while Zhen and Yu offered clear judgment in regulation and example—they none dishonored their duties, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Qun, Xu Xuan, Wei Zhen, and Lu Yu held those chairs longest; Chen Jiao and Xu Xuan were flint-spined, while Wei Zhen and Lu Yu policed the machinery with cool judgment—none, it is said, disgraced his charge.
